Take-home line
“Where is your brother Abel?”
live: Walk the Way of the Cross
Join your parish for the Way of the Cross this evening, or pray it at home with your family.
Be your brother's keeper (Genesis 4:9)
Visit or call one relative or neighbour you have neglected, and ask what they need.
2027-02-12.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, your blood speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. Master the sin that lurks at the door of our hearts, take the log from our eyes, and make us keepers of our brothers and sisters. Give us the faith of Abraham, hoping against hope, and lead us through the waters of these days to your Easter. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we receive the Blood of Christ, which does not cry for vengeance like Abel's but for mercy and peace.

2027-02-13.title: First Saturday of the Great Fast
2027-02-13.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-02-13.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-13.verse: And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.
theo: On Thursday Paul left us with every mouth silenced: no one is righteous, not even one. Today he opens a door: “But now, apart from law, the righteousness of God has been disclosed, and is attested by the law and the prophets, the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe.” The sentence that follows is one of the most important in the New Testament: “since all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God put forward as a sacrifice of atonement by his blood, effective through faith.” This matters at the end of the first week of the Great Fast. We do not buy God's favour with our fasting. Grace comes first, freely, through the blood of Christ. Our fasting, prayer and almsgiving are our response to that gift, and grace itself makes them fruitful. Whoever forgets this turns the fast into a ledger of achievements; whoever remembers it fasts with gratitude.

The Gospel gives us the prayer that holds the whole Great Fast together: “Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come. Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And do not bring us to the time of trial, but rescue us from the evil one.” The Holy Qurbana of our Church opens with this prayer and returns to it before Communion. Each line is a Lenten programme: God's name first, his kingdom before our plans, bread asked for one day at a time by people who are fasting, forgiveness given and received, and rescue in the time of trial, as Jesus himself was tested in the wilderness. Of all the petitions, Jesus comments on only one: “For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.” The week that began with the gift left before the altar ends with the same lesson: the forgiven must forgive.
outline: Opening
Ask: which line of the Our Father is hardest for you to pray honestly?
Point 1 · Justified as a gift
All have sinned; grace comes first.
Point 2 · Our Father
The Lord's Prayer as a Lenten programme.
Point 3 · As we forgive
The one petition Jesus explains.
Take-home line
“And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
live: Pray it slowly (Matthew 6:9–13)
Pray the Our Father once today very slowly, pausing a full minute on each petition.
Forgive as you are forgiven (Matthew 6:14)
Name before God one person you forgive, and go to confession this Saturday if you can.
2027-02-13.prayer: Our Father in heaven, all of us have sinned and fallen short of your glory, and you justify us freely by your grace in Christ Jesus. Let us fast with gratitude and not with pride. Hallow your name in us, bring your kingdom, give us today our daily bread, forgive us as we forgive, and rescue us from the evil one. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we pray the Our Father before Communion: forgiven and forgiving, we receive the Bread of life.

2027-02-15.title: Second Monday of the Great Fast
2027-02-15.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-02-15.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-15.verse: there is nothing outside a person that by going in can defile, but the things that come out are what defile.
theo: The second week of the Great Fast opens with a Gospel that seems, at first hearing, to argue against fasting. Jesus calls the crowd and says: “Listen to me, all of you, and understand: there is nothing outside a person that by going in can defile, but the things that come out are what defile.” Mark even adds his own comment: “Thus he declared all foods clean.” Older members of many St Thomas Christian families remember a Great Fast kept without meat, fish, eggs or milk, and some households still keep it so; in earlier generations many took only one full meal a day. Why, then, do we give up food that Jesus himself called clean? Not because the fish curry is unclean. We fast because the stomach is a good teacher of the heart. The one who learns to say no to a plate learns, little by little, to say no to the anger, the envy and the greed that come out of the heart. The Church fasts from clean things in order to become clean within.

Jesus names what really defiles. “For it is from within, from the human heart, that evil intentions come: fornication, theft, murder, adultery, avarice, wickedness, deceit, licentiousness, envy, slander, pride, folly. All these evil things come from within, and they defile a person.” It is an uncomfortable list, and it is honest. Nobody needs to be taught envy or pride; they grow in the heart like weeds in a compound left alone for one monsoon. The wise of Israel said: “Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life.” A fast that watches the kitchen but not the heart has guarded the wrong door. That is why many of our elders spoke of fasting with the tongue too: no gossip, no cursing, no sharp word at the dinner table, for as long as the fast lasts.

Paul's letter to Titus gives the other half of the answer. We cannot clean the heart by our own scrubbing. Paul describes believers as they once were, “foolish, disobedient, led astray, slaves to various passions and pleasures, passing our days in malice and envy.” “But when the goodness and loving kindness of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit.” The heart is washed in baptism and renewed by the Spirit poured out “richly”. Fasting does not buy this grace; it makes room for it. So Paul can ask for a very ordinary holiness, the kind that shows in a neighbourhood: “to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarreling, to be gentle, and to show every courtesy to everyone.” This week, let the fast reach the heart, and let the heart reach the street.
outline: Opening
Ask: if Jesus declared all foods clean, why do we still fast?
Point 1 · Fasting from clean things
The stomach as a teacher of the heart.
Point 2 · From within
The list of what really defiles.
Point 3 · Washed and renewed
God's kindness appeared; the Spirit poured out richly.
Point 4 · Holiness in the street
Speak evil of no one, be gentle with everyone.
Take-home line
“there is nothing outside a person that by going in can defile, but the things that come out are what defile.”
live: A fast of the tongue (Titus 3:2)
For the rest of this week, speak evil of no one, not even in jest; if you slip, say a short prayer for the person you spoke about.
Guard the heart (Mark 7:21)
Each night before sleep, look back on the day and ask which of Jesus' list came out of your heart today.
Remember your baptism (Titus 3:5)
Find out the date of your baptism and thank God for it in your family prayer.
2027-02-15.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you see the heart and you know what comes out of it. Let our fasting from food become a fasting from envy, slander and pride. By the water of rebirth you have washed us; pour out your Spirit on us richly again, so that our words may be gentle and our hearts clean. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we ask to approach the holy mysteries with a clean heart; the Lord who washed us in baptism feeds us now, so that what comes out of us may be his goodness.

2027-02-16.title: Second Tuesday of the Great Fast
2027-02-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The glory that is to be revealed
2027-02-16.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-16.verse: “Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
theo: February in Kerala is the beginning of the hot months. The paddy fields of the Kole lands and Kuttanad lie dry after the harvest, the wells begin to fall, and by the afternoon the whole land seems to wait for a rain that will not come until the summer showers. Paul gives words to that waiting. “I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory about to be revealed to us. For the creation waits with eager longing for the revealing of the children of God.” Creation was subjected to futility, “in hope that the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to decay and will obtain the freedom of the glory of the children of God.” Then comes one of the boldest images in Scripture: “We know that the whole creation has been groaning in labor pains until now.” The groan of the world is not the cry of a dying thing, but of a mother about to give birth.

We groan too. “And not only the creation, but we ourselves, who have the first fruits of the Spirit, groan inwardly while we wait for adoption, the redemption of our bodies.” The Great Fast teaches us to feel this groan honestly. When we are hungry in the late afternoon, when a habit we have given up pulls at us, when prayer feels dry, we are standing with the whole creation in its labour. Paul does not call this despair; he calls it hope. “For in hope we were saved. Now hope that is seen is not hope. For who hopes for what is seen? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience.” Many parishes hold their Lenten retreat, the dhyanam, in these weeks, and families come back from those days of listening with the same discovery: the waiting itself is a school of hope.

Into this waiting Jesus speaks his invitation to pray. “Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.” He is not describing a vending machine, but a father. “Is there anyone among you who, if your child asks for bread, will give a stone? Or if the child asks for a fish, will give a snake? If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!” The Father does not always give what we name, but he never gives a stone for bread. And the same passage ends with the golden rule: “In everything do to others as you would have them do to you; for this is the law and the prophets.” The one who knocks at God's door learns to open his own door to others.
outline: Opening
Ask: what are you waiting for, and how do you wait?
Point 1 · Creation in labour
The groan of the world is a birth pang.
Point 2 · Saved in hope
We wait with patience for what we do not see.
Point 3 · Ask, search, knock
A Father who never gives a stone for bread.
Point 4 · The golden rule
The one who knocks learns to open.
Take-home line
“Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.”
live: Keep asking (Matthew 7:7)
Choose one intention and bring it to God every day for the rest of the Great Fast, without giving up.
Do to others (Matthew 7:12)
Each evening this week, ask: did I treat someone today as I would want to be treated?
Care for creation (Romans 8:21)
Save water this summer and share it generously with neighbours whose wells run dry.
2027-02-16.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, with the whole creation we groan and wait for the glory to come. Teach us to hope for what we do not see and to wait for it with patience. You told us to ask, to search and to knock; give us the confidence of children before the Father who never gives a stone for bread, and make us generous to others as we want them to be to us. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Father gives us the true bread from heaven; we receive in hope the first fruits of the glory that is still to be revealed.

2027-02-17.title: Second Wednesday of the Great Fast
2027-02-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Eternal life is the gift of God
2027-02-17.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-17.verse: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
theo: The Gospel begins with a group of people we never meet by name. Jesus crosses the lake to his own town, Capernaum, “and just then some people were carrying a paralyzed man lying on a bed.” The man cannot walk to Jesus; others must carry him. Matthew notes something remarkable: “When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, ‘Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.’” It is the faith of the carriers that Jesus sees. In many of our parishes, during the Great Fast, the priest goes from house to house to hear the confessions of the sick and the elderly and to bring them Holy Communion; in others the young people bring the housebound to church for the penitential service, in wheelchairs, in autorickshaws, sometimes on a chair carried by four. Every such journey repeats this Gospel. Some of us walk to Christ; some of us must be carried; and some of us are called to carry.

Then comes the surprise. The friends had brought the man for his legs, but Jesus speaks first about his sins. The scribes are scandalised: “This man is blaspheming.” Only God can forgive sins, and they are right about that. Jesus answers their unspoken thoughts: “Which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Stand up and walk’? But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins” he said to the paralytic, “Stand up, take your bed and go to your home.” The visible healing proves the invisible one. The deepest paralysis is the one that keeps us from God, and Jesus heals that first. The crowd's response is full of meaning for us: “they glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.” The authority to forgive, which belongs to God alone, Christ has placed in human hands. On Easter evening he will breathe on his apostles and say: “If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them.” Every confession heard in a Kerala parish this Lent stands on this verse.

Paul tells us what forgiveness is for. It is not a licence to go on sinning: “Should we sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means!” The forgiven are set free, not to belong to nobody, but to belong to God. “For just as you once presented your members as slaves to impurity and to greater and greater iniquity, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness for sanctification.” The man in the Gospel rose and carried the bed that had carried him. So it is with us: the members of our body that once served sin, the hands, the eyes, the tongue, are now to serve holiness. And the end of this road is not wages but a gift: “the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
outline: Opening
Ask: who carried you to Christ, and whom are you carrying?
Point 1 · Carried by faith
Jesus saw their faith.
Point 2 · Your sins are forgiven
The deepest paralysis healed first.
Point 3 · Authority given to human beings
From Capernaum to the confessional.
Point 4 · Members for holiness
Rise, take up the bed, and serve righteousness.
Take-home line
“Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
live: Carry someone (Matthew 9:2)
Offer to bring an elderly or sick person to church, or ask the parish priest to visit someone housebound for confession this Lent.
Go to confession (John 20:23)
If you have not yet made your Lenten confession, fix the day now.
Members for holiness (Romans 6:19)
Choose one part of your body that has served sin, your eyes, your tongue or your hands, and give it a work of holiness every day this week.
2027-02-17.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you saw the faith of those who carried the paralysed man and you forgave his sins. Give us friends who carry us to you, and make us friends who carry others. Thank you for giving to human beings the authority to forgive in your name. Raise us from every paralysis of sin, and let us present our members to you for holiness. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Before Holy Communion we pray as sinners who need healing; the Lord who forgave the paralysed man forgives us in the sacrament of reconciliation and feeds us at his table, so that we may rise and walk.

2027-02-18.title: Second Thursday of the Great Fast
2027-02-18.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The justice and faithfulness of God
2027-02-18.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-18.verse: Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.
theo: Paul asks a hard question in today's epistle. If God chose Israel and entrusted them with “the oracles of God”, what happens when some of them prove unfaithful? “What if some were unfaithful? Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? By no means! Although everyone is a liar, let God be proved true.” This is the rock under the whole Great Fast. We come to these weeks aware of promises we have broken: baptismal promises, marriage promises, resolutions made last Lent and forgotten by Easter Tuesday. Our faithlessness is real, but it does not cancel God's faithfulness. He keeps his word when we do not keep ours. The prophet who sat among the ruins of Jerusalem could still say: “The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.”

Paul then refuses a clever argument. Some said: if our sin only makes God's justice and mercy shine more brightly, why not sin more? “Let us do evil so that good may come”? Paul's answer is short: “Their condemnation is deserved!” The Church has kept this as a firm rule of the moral life: we may never do evil so that good may result from it (Catechism 1789). A lie told to save face, a bribe paid to get a good thing done quickly, a small dishonesty in the accounts for the sake of the family: the end does not wash the means. God's mercy is not an excuse for sin; it is the door out of it.

Jesus applies this faithfulness to our ordinary speech. The old law said, do not swear falsely, and fulfil the vows you made to the Lord. “But I say to you, Do not swear at all, either by heaven, for it is the throne of God, or by the earth, for it is his footstool, or by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King. And do not swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.” We know this speech well in Kerala. “Ammayaane sathyam”, by my mother it is true; “daivathaane”, by God; a hand placed on a child's head to make a word believable. The very need to add an oath shows that our plain word is not trusted. The Church understands that Jesus does not forbid every oath, for an oath may be taken for a grave and just reason, as in a court of law (Catechism 2154). What he asks is that we become people whose word needs no support. “Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.” The same is true of the vows and nerchas we make to God in times of need: let them be few, sincere and kept. A fast that makes us more truthful has already begun to make us like God, whose yes is always yes.
outline: Opening
Ask: if you said something today without any oath, would people believe you?
Point 1 · God is faithful
Our faithlessness does not cancel his faithfulness.
Point 2 · Not evil that good may come
The end does not wash the means.
Point 3 · Do not swear
By my mother, by God, by my child's head.
Point 4 · Yes, yes; no, no
Becoming people whose word needs no support.
Take-home line
“Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’.”
live: No oaths this week (Matthew 5:34)
Do not add “by God” or “by my mother” to anything you say this week; let your plain word stand.
Keep a broken promise (Romans 3:3)
Remember one promise you made and did not keep, and keep it now, or apologise for breaking it.
No small dishonesty (Romans 3:8)
Look honestly at your work, your accounts and your bills; correct one small dishonesty this Lent.
2027-02-18.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, your Father is faithful even when we are faithless, and his mercies are new every morning. Free us from every lie and from the temptation to do evil so that good may come. Make our speech simple and true, our yes a yes and our no a no, and let our vows to you be sincere and faithfully kept. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana God keeps his promise to be with us always; our Amen at Holy Communion is a yes that should mean yes for the whole day.

2027-02-19.title: Second Friday of the Great Fast
2027-02-19.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The commandment of God is holy and just
2027-02-19.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). Abstinence from meat; fasting is highly recommended. Way of the Cross.
2027-02-19.verse: Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.
theo: The first reading shows us sin from God's side. “The LORD saw that the wickedness of humankind was great in the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of their hearts was only evil continually. And the LORD was sorry that he had made humankind on the earth, and it grieved him to his heart.” We usually think of sin as breaking a rule. Genesis shows it as wounding a heart. The earth “was filled with violence”, and God grieves like a father who watches his children destroy one another. Yet one sentence opens a door: “But Noah found favor in the sight of the LORD.” “Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.” On a Friday of the Great Fast, when we stand before the Cross, we see how far that grief of God went. The heart that was grieved in Genesis is the heart pierced on Calvary.

The second reading is a story of new beginnings at Gilgal. The generation that left Egypt had died in the wilderness, “not having listened to the voice of the LORD.” Their children, born on the journey, are circumcised at Gilgal, and God says: “Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.” Then they keep the Passover, and the next day they eat the produce of the land, and “the manna ceased.” The food of the journey gives way to the food of the promised land. During these weeks, and above all around Holy Week, thousands of pilgrims climb the hill of Malayattoor, where tradition remembers St Thomas at prayer. Many go barefoot, some carry wooden crosses, and the slope rings with the old cry, “Ponnin Kurishu Muthappo, ponmala kayattam.” A pilgrimage is a small Gilgal: we carry the disgrace of our old slavery up the hill, and the Lord rolls it away. Paul adds that the law itself was never the problem: “So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and just and good.” The commandment “You shall not covet” showed Paul his sin, and sin used even the good commandment to deceive him. The law names the illness; only Christ heals it.

In the Gospel the leaders in the temple ask Jesus, “By what authority are you doing these things? Who gave you this authority to do them?” Jesus answers with a question about John's baptism. They calculate: if we say from heaven, he will ask why we did not believe; if we say of human origin, the crowd will turn on us. So they answer: “We do not know.” It is not ignorance; it is refusal. They did know, but they would not say it, because the answer would have asked them to change. Many of our evasions in confession and in prayer sound just like this: I do not know. The Great Fast is the time to stop calculating, to admit what we already know, and to let the Lord roll away our disgrace.
outline: Opening
Ask: what does my sin do to the heart of God?
Point 1 · It grieved him to his heart
Sin seen from God's side; Noah who walked with God.
Point 2 · Disgrace rolled away
Gilgal, the Passover, and the end of the manna.
Point 3 · The law is holy
It names the illness; Christ heals it.
Point 4 · We do not know
The evasion that refuses to change.
Take-home line
“Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt.”
live: Stand before the Cross (Genesis 6:6)
Make the Way of the Cross today, at church or at home, and at the twelfth station tell the Lord you are sorry for having grieved his heart.
Name it honestly (Mark 11:33)
In your next confession, do not say “I do not know”; name plainly the sin you already know.
A small pilgrimage (Joshua 5:9)
Plan a pilgrimage this Lent, to Malayattoor or to a shrine near you, and offer it for someone carrying a disgrace.
2027-02-19.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, our sins grieved the heart of your Father, and on the Cross your own heart was pierced for us. Roll away from us the disgrace of our old slavery, as you did for Israel at Gilgal. Give us the honesty to say what we know, and the courage to change. Feed us on our journey until we reach the land you have promised. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Israel kept the Passover at Gilgal and the manna ceased; in the Holy Qurbana Christ our Passover is offered, and he is the bread for our journey until we eat with him in the kingdom.

2027-02-20.title: Second Saturday of the Great Fast
2027-02-20.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-02-20.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-20.verse: Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.
theo: Jesus looks at his generation and sees children playing in the bazaar. “It is like children sitting in the marketplaces and calling to one another, ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we wailed, and you did not mourn.’” One group wants to play wedding, the other wants to play funeral, and nobody joins anybody. So it was with John and Jesus. “For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon’; the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’” John's fasting was too strict for them; Jesus' table fellowship was too free. The real problem was neither the fast nor the feast. It was a heart that had decided in advance not to respond to God, whatever music he played.

There is a lesson here for the Great Fast. The Church plays both tunes in her year. Now she sings the lament of the fast; at Easter she will play the flute of the Resurrection and call us to dance. Ecclesiastes says there is “a time to mourn, and a time to dance”. The danger is to be the child who does neither: who keeps the outward forms of the fast without sorrow for sin, and who will keep the Easter feast without joy in the Risen Lord. Many men in our parishes take a pledge during the Great Fast to give up alcohol and smoking, and their friends sometimes mock them for it; and when those same men come to the Easter table with joy, someone else will find fault. Jesus' answer is quiet and final: “Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.” Do not argue with the mockers. Let the fruit of the fast speak.

Paul's letter deals with a painful situation in the Church of Corinth, where a member was living in open sexual sin and the community had done nothing. He clarifies an earlier instruction: he did not mean that Christians must avoid every immoral person in the world, “since you would then need to go out of the world.” He means the Church must not pretend that open and unrepented sin among her own members is normal. “For what have I to do with judging those outside? Is it not those who are inside that you are to judge? God will judge those outside.” This is not a licence for gossip or contempt. Earlier in the same chapter Paul says the aim is that the sinner's “spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord.” The Great Fast turns this word first towards ourselves: “But if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.” Before we sit in judgment on the world outside, the Church, and each of us within it, must look honestly at our own house.
outline: Opening
Ask: when God calls, do I dance or mourn, or do I do neither?
Point 1 · Children in the bazaar
A heart that has decided not to respond.
Point 2 · A time to mourn, a time to dance
The fast now, the feast at Easter.
Point 3 · Wisdom vindicated by her deeds
Let the fruit of the fast answer the mockers.
Point 4 · Judge those inside
Self-examination before judging the world.
Take-home line
“Yet wisdom is vindicated by her deeds.”
live: Give up a harmful habit (1 Corinthians 5:11)
If you drink or smoke, give it up for the rest of the Great Fast, and give the money saved to a family in need.
Do not answer the mockers (Matthew 11:19)
When someone laughs at your fast or your faith this week, answer with a kind deed instead of an argument.
Judge yourself first (1 Corinthians 11:31)
Before saying anything critical about another person or about the Church, ask what needs correcting in yourself.
2027-02-20.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you came to us in the fasting of John and in your own table shared with sinners, and many would not respond. Do not let our hearts be like children who will neither dance nor mourn. Give us true sorrow in this fast and true joy at Easter. Free us from every habit that enslaves us, teach us to judge ourselves before we judge others, and let our deeds show your wisdom. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Jesus was called a friend of tax collectors and sinners; at the Holy Qurbana that friend invites sinners to his table, and those who come with repentant hearts go away rejoicing.

2027-02-22.title: Third Monday of the Great Fast
2027-02-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Serving in the newness of the Spirit
2027-02-22.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). In the Latin calendar today is the feast of the Chair of St Peter.
2027-02-22.verse: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.
theo: The third week of the Great Fast is often the hardest. The first fervour has cooled, Easter is still far off, and the fast can quietly turn into a list of rules kept with a tight jaw. Paul speaks straight into that danger. He uses an image his readers knew well: a married woman is bound to her husband while he lives, but if he dies she is free. In the same way, he says, “you have died to the law through the body of Christ, so that you may belong to another, to him who has been raised from the dead in order that we may bear fruit for God.” The old life produced fruit “for death”; the new life belongs to the risen Christ. And he sums it up: “But now we are discharged from the law, dead to that which held us captive, so that we are slaves not under the old written code but in the new life of the Spirit.” Our fasting can be kept in either way. It can be the old written code, counted and checked like a ledger, or it can be the new life of the Spirit, a heart that gives up small things because it belongs to Someone. In many parishes these weeks bring the Lenten retreat, the dhyanam: a few evenings of preaching, adoration and confession, when people who seldom come to church find a place at the back. Its whole purpose is to move us from the ledger to the Spirit.

In the Gospel a scribe, impressed by Jesus' answers, asks the question every religious person must face: “Which commandment is the first of all?” Jesus answers with the prayer every pious Jew said morning and evening: “Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one; you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.” He adds a second, which no one had asked for: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” The scribe agrees wholeheartedly; to love God and neighbour, he says, “is much more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.” Jesus looks at him and says, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” Not far is a beautiful word and also a warning. One can know the right answer and still stand at the door. The fast is not a burnt offering by which we pay God; it clears the heart so that love may have room. The Latin Church keeps today the feast of the Chair of St Peter, the apostle whose whole authority rests on one answer given by the lake: “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you” (John 21:15).
outline: Opening
Ask: is my fast a ledger, or a love?
Point 1 · Not under the old written code
Dead to the law, alive to Christ.
Point 2 · With all your heart
The first commandment and the second.
Point 3 · Not far from the kingdom
Knowing the answer and stepping inside.
Take-home line
“You are not far from the kingdom of God.”
live: Pray the Shema (Mark 12:29–30)
Say the first commandment slowly each morning this week, and let it decide one choice of the day.
Join the retreat
If your parish has a Lenten retreat, attend at least one evening, and bring someone who has stayed away.
2027-02-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you have freed us from the old written code and given us the new life of the Spirit. Do not let our fast become a ledger of rules, but a love that gives itself. Teach us to love the Father with all our heart, soul, mind and strength, and our neighbour as ourselves, and do not leave us standing near the door of your kingdom, but bring us in. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the two commandments meet: we offer ourselves to the Father with Christ, and we receive the Bread that makes us one body with our neighbours.

2027-02-23.title: Third Tuesday of the Great Fast
2027-02-23.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Whoever thinks he stands, let him not fall
2027-02-23.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). St Polycarp, bishop and martyr, is remembered today in the Latin calendar.
2027-02-23.verse: So if you think you are standing, watch out that you do not fall.
theo: Paul looks back at Israel in the desert and sees a mirror of the baptised. “Our ancestors were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea, and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea, and all ate the same spiritual food, and all drank the same spiritual drink.” He even says of the water from the rock: “the rock was Christ.” Every privilege was theirs, and yet “God was not pleased with most of them, and they were struck down in the wilderness.” They craved, they turned to idols, they tested God, they grumbled. Paul does not tell the story to frighten the Corinthians but to wake them: “These things happened to them to serve as an example, and they were written down to instruct us, on whom the ends of the ages have come.” We too have passed through the water of baptism and eat the spiritual food of the Holy Qurbana. These gifts do not make us safe if we stop watching. Hence the sober line: “So if you think you are standing, watch out that you do not fall.” But Paul never leaves a warning without a promise: “No testing has overtaken you that is not common to everyone. God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength, but with the testing he will also provide the way out so that you may be able to endure it.” In the third week of the fast, when we too are tempted to grumble in the desert, that promise is worth learning by heart.

In the Gospel Jesus points to the fig tree: when it puts out leaves, everyone knows summer is near. The signs of God's kingdom are just as plain for those who look. “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.” Then comes a very practical warning: “Be on guard so that your hearts are not weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and the worries of this life, and that day does not catch you unexpectedly, like a trap.” Three things make the heart heavy: too much pleasure, too much drink, too much worry. The Church in Kerala has long urged the faithful to keep the Great Fast free of alcohol, and many men who drink keep these fifty days dry; for some it has been the beginning of freedom. Jesus' last word is a programme for the whole fast: “Be alert at all times, praying that you may have the strength to escape all these things that will take place, and to stand before the Son of Man.” The Latin calendar remembers today St Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna and disciple of the apostle John, who after eighty-six years of serving Christ refused to deny him and was put to death. He was able to stand at the end because he had watched and prayed all his life.
outline: Opening
Ask: where do I think I am standing safely?
Point 1 · Written down to instruct us
Israel in the desert, a mirror for the baptised.
Point 2 · God is faithful
No testing beyond our strength; a way out.
Point 3 · Be alert at all times
Hearts not weighed down; praying for strength.
Take-home line
“So if you think you are standing, watch out that you do not fall.”
live: Lighten the heart (Luke 21:34)
Name the one thing that weighs your heart down most, pleasure, drink or worry, and take one step against it today.
Learn the promise (1 Corinthians 10:13)
Memorise “God is faithful” and say it the next time temptation comes.
2027-02-23.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the rock that followed your people in the desert, and you feed us with spiritual food. Keep us from grumbling and from false security; do not let our hearts grow heavy with pleasure, drink or worry. When we are tested, show us the way out, and through the prayers of St Polycarp give us strength to stand before you at the end. Amen.
altar: The spiritual food and drink of the desert were a figure; at the Holy Qurbana Christ himself, the true rock, gives us his Body and Blood for the journey.

2027-02-24.title: Third Wednesday of the Great Fast
2027-02-24.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Do not repay evil for evil, but repay with a blessing
2027-02-24.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-24.verse: But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
theo: Peter writes to small Christian communities scattered across Asia Minor, minorities who were mocked, slandered and sometimes threatened by their neighbours. He does not teach them how to hit back. He describes a community: “Finally, all of you, have unity of spirit, sympathy, love for one another, a tender heart, and a humble mind.” Then the hard part: “Do not repay evil for evil or abuse for abuse; but, on the contrary, repay with a blessing.” The world runs on the law of return: you insult me, I insult you; you ignore me, I ignore you. Peter asks Christians to break the circle by returning something better than what they received. He reminds them that blessing is their own calling, “that you might inherit a blessing”, and he quotes the psalm: “let them keep their tongues from evil and their lips from speaking deceit; let them turn away from evil and do good; let them seek peace and pursue it.” Peace is not something we wait for; it has to be pursued, like someone running after a friend who has walked away. The Great Fast is a fast of the tongue as well as of the stomach. A day without meat is easy compared with a day without a sharp reply.

In the Gospel Jesus goes further still: “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous.” Kerala knows this picture well: when the rain comes it falls on every compound, on the house of the saint and the house of the sinner, on the field of the friend and the field of the enemy. That is how God loves. “For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?” Love that only returns love is ordinary; Christian love begins where the return stops. Then the summit of the Sermon: “Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.” Perfect here means whole, a love with no one left out. We may not feel love for an enemy, but we can pray for him, and prayer is where love begins. Jesus himself prayed from the Cross for those who crucified him: “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing” (Luke 23:34). Tomorrow the Syro-Malabar Church honours a daughter of Kerala whose family lived these words to the end.
outline: Opening
Ask: who is the person I find hardest to bless?
Point 1 · Repay with a blessing
Breaking the circle of return.
Point 2 · Seek peace and pursue it
The fast of the tongue.
Point 3 · Love your enemies
Sun and rain on the evil and the good.
Point 4 · Perfect as your Father
A love with no one left out.
Take-home line
“Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
live: Pray by name (Matthew 5:44)
Write down the name of one person who has hurt you, and pray for that person every evening until Easter.
Fast from the sharp reply (1 Peter 3:9)
Today, when you are insulted or ignored, answer with a blessing or with silence.
2027-02-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, from the Cross you prayed for those who crucified you. Give us a tender heart and a humble mind, teach us not to repay evil for evil but to answer with a blessing, and make us children of the Father who sends his sun and rain on all. Make our love whole, with no one left out, and give us peace to pursue and to share. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we receive the Body of the Lord who gave himself for his enemies; we cannot receive him and refuse to pray for ours.

2027-02-25.title: Third Thursday of the Great Fast · Blessed Rani Maria
2027-02-25.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The Lord rewards every good deed
2027-02-25.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). Blessed Rani Maria, martyr: Genesis 22:1–13; 2 Maccabees 7:1–11; 2 Corinthians 4:7–15; Matthew 10:16–25.
2027-02-25.verse: Render service with enthusiasm, as to the Lord and not to men and women, knowing that whatever good we do, we will receive the same again from the Lord, whether we are slaves or free.
theo: Paul's letter to the Ephesians walks into the ordinary household of his time: parents and children, masters and slaves. To children he says, “Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right”, and he recalls the commandment, “Honor your father and mother.” To fathers he gives a warning that every parent needs: “do not provoke your children to anger, but bring them up in the discipline and instruction of the Lord.” To slaves and masters he speaks in a world where slavery was taken for granted, and he plants a seed that would one day break it open: “you know that both of you have the same Master in heaven, and with him there is no partiality.” The key to the whole passage is one phrase: work done “as to the Lord.” Every service, in the kitchen, the office, the field or the hospital ward, can be offered to Christ, “knowing that whatever good we do, we will receive the same again from the Lord.” In the Gospel Jesus shows the opposite. He has just reminded the crowd that David himself calls the Messiah “Lord”, and the people listen “with delight”. Then he warns them: “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, and to be greeted with respect in the marketplaces, and to have the best seats in the synagogues and places of honor at banquets! They devour widows' houses and for the sake of appearance say long prayers.” Religion can be used for honour and profit. Even a fast can be kept for appearance. Jesus asks for service that seeks no seat of honour and that protects the widow instead of devouring her house.

Today the Syro-Malabar Church keeps the memory of Blessed Rani Maria, who lived exactly that kind of service. Mariam Vattalil was born in 1954 at Pulluvazhy near Perumbavoor, joined the Franciscan Clarist Congregation and received the name Rani Maria. She served in mission stations in North India, and from 1992 at Udainagar in the diocese of Indore. There she worked among poor tribal families: she helped them to learn, to save, to form groups, to know their rights and to free themselves from moneylenders who held them in debt. This angered those who profited from their poverty. On 25 February 1995, as she travelled by bus towards Indore, a man hired by them attacked her with a knife, and she died of her wounds by the roadside. She was forty-one. Her readings today speak of her: “See, I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves”, and “we have this treasure in clay jars, so that it may be made clear that this extraordinary power belongs to God and does not come from us.” What followed is a Gospel in itself. Her killer, Samundar Singh, was sentenced to prison, and there he came to repentance. Her sister, Sr Selmy, also a Clarist sister, visited him and tied a rakhi on his wrist, accepting him as her brother, and her parents received him in their home as a son. On 4 November 2017 Rani Maria was beatified at Indore, the first woman martyr from India to be declared Blessed. Like the mother in the book of Maccabees, her family showed that the love of God is stronger than death and stronger than hatred.
outline: Opening
Ask: for whom do I really work, and whom do I serve?
Point 1 · As to the Lord
Service in the home and at work offered to Christ.
Point 2 · Long robes and widows' houses
Religion for show, and religion that protects the poor.
Point 3 · Sheep among wolves
Blessed Rani Maria at Udainagar.
Point 4 · Treasure in clay jars
A martyr's blood and a family's forgiveness.
Take-home line
“Render service with enthusiasm, as to the Lord.”
live: Work as to the Lord (Ephesians 6:7)
Offer today's work to Christ before you begin it, and do one task well that no one will notice.
Protect the poor (Mark 12:40)
Support, with money or time, one group that frees poor families from debt or exploitation.
2027-02-25.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you came not to be served but to serve, and you protected the widow and the poor. Teach us to work as to you, without seeking honour, and to stand with the poor against those who devour their homes. Through the prayers of Blessed Rani Maria, who served the poor and gave her life for you, give us courage among wolves and a forgiveness stronger than hatred. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we offer the treasure we carry in clay jars: our ordinary work and lives, joined to the sacrifice of Christ, who gave his life for those who killed him.

2027-02-26.title: Third Friday of the Great Fast
2027-02-26.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The mind set on the Spirit is life
2027-02-26.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). A Friday of abstinence from meat; the Way of the Cross is prayed in parishes and homes.
2027-02-26.verse: There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
theo: After the flood God speaks to Noah and binds himself by a promise, not only to Noah's family but “with every living creature that is with you, the birds, the domestic animals, and every animal of the earth with you.” He gives a sign: “I have set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.” The Hebrew word for the rainbow is the same as for a warrior's bow; God hangs up his weapon in the sky. And the sign is for God himself: “When the bow is in the clouds, I will see it and remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living creature of all flesh that is on the earth.” God binds himself to remember. The second reading tells how the walls of Jericho fell, not by siege engines but by obedience. Seven priests with seven trumpets walk before the ark, around the city, once a day for six days, and the people are told: “You shall not shout or let your voice be heard, nor shall you utter a word, until the day I tell you to shout.” On the seventh day they go round seven times; the trumpets sound, the people shout, “and the wall fell down flat.” Rahab and her family are spared “because she hid the messengers”. These pages of conquest are hard to read, and the Church reads them in the light of Christ, not as a pattern for treating people but as a picture of the walls of sin that fall before patient, silent obedience. During these weeks pilgrims climb Malayattoor hill, where tradition says St Thomas prayed, many carrying wooden crosses, step after step, calling on the golden cross. Like the circling of Jericho, Lenten prayer is often slow and repeated, and its fruit comes on a day we do not choose.

Paul opens the eighth chapter of Romans with the most freeing sentence a sinner can hear: “There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.” What the law could not do, God did, “by sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh.” The choice before us is a matter of where we set our minds: “To set the mind on the flesh is death, but to set the mind on the Spirit is life and peace.” In the Gospel the Sadducees, who deny the resurrection, bring Jesus a riddle about a woman married in turn to seven brothers: whose wife will she be? Jesus answers: “Is not this the reason you are wrong, that you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God?” The risen life is not this life repeated; it is new. And he goes back to the burning bush, where God called himself the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, long after they had died: “He is God not of the dead, but of the living.” On this Friday we walk the Way of the Cross to the tomb, but the tomb is not the end of the road. Those we have lost are alive to God, and we pray for them in that hope.
outline: Opening
Ask: what wall in my life has not yet fallen?
Point 1 · The bow in the clouds
God binds himself to remember.
Point 2 · Seven days around Jericho
Patient, silent obedience.
Point 3 · No condemnation
The mind set on the Spirit is life and peace.
Point 4 · God of the living
The resurrection and our dead.
Take-home line
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
live: Walk and keep silence (Joshua 6:10)
Pray the Way of the Cross today with as little talk as possible before and after.
Pray for the dead (Mark 12:27)
Name the departed of your family at the end of today's prayer, and visit their graves if you can.
2027-02-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, in you there is no condemnation. Remember your everlasting covenant with us, as you remembered Noah; bring down the walls of our sin through patient obedience; set our minds on the Spirit, who gives life and peace. You are God of the living: give eternal rest to our departed and bring us all to the resurrection. Amen.
altar: The rainbow was the sign of the covenant with Noah; at the Holy Qurbana Christ gives us the cup of the new covenant in his blood, and God remembers us for ever.

2027-02-27.title: Third Saturday of the Great Fast
2027-02-27.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The evils to be put away
The kingdom of God belongs to those who repent
2027-02-27.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-27.verse: and be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.
theo: Paul writes about the most ordinary place of holiness: the way we talk to one another. “So then, putting away falsehood, let all of us speak the truth to our neighbors, for we are members of one another.” A lie told to a brother is like one hand deceiving the other. Then a realistic word about anger: “Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger, and do not make room for the devil.” Anger is not always sin, but anger kept overnight becomes a room rented to the devil. The thief is not only to stop stealing but to work honestly “so as to have something to share with the needy.” And speech is to build up: “Let no evil talk come out of your mouths, but only what is useful for building up, as there is need, so that your words may give grace to those who hear.” Paul reminds the baptised that they carry a seal: “do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, with which you were marked with a seal for the day of redemption.” The Holy Spirit is grieved by bitterness at the dinner table as much as by great crimes. Many Syro-Malabar families keep a beautiful custom that answers this word: after the night prayer the children greet their parents and elders, “Praise be to Jesus Christ”, and receive the answer, “Now and for ever, Amen.” It is hard to go to sleep angry after saying that. Paul ends with the verse that could be written over every Christian home: “Put away from you all bitterness and wrath and anger and wrangling and slander, together with all malice, and be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”

In the Gospel Jesus tells a short parable in the temple. A father asks his two sons to work in the vineyard. One says, “I will not”; but later he changed his mind and went. The other answers politely, “I go, sir”; but he did not go. “Which of the two did the will of his father?” The answer is obvious, and it is aimed at people who had always said yes to God with their lips. “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.” They had said no to God for years, but when John came preaching repentance, they changed their minds and believed. The religious leaders saw it happen, “and even after you saw it, you did not change your minds and believe him.” The parable has two warnings and one hope. Saying yes is not the same as going; and a past no is not the last word. The Great Fast is the time of “later he changed his mind.” On Saturday evenings in these weeks, the queues for confession grow longer in many parishes. Every person standing in that line is the son who once said no, and is now going into the vineyard.
outline: Opening
Ask: where have I said yes to God and not gone?
Point 1 · Members of one another
Truth, anger and the setting sun.
Point 2 · Words that give grace
Do not grieve the Holy Spirit.
Point 3 · Two sons
Yes without going, and no that turns into yes.
Take-home line
“be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ has forgiven you.”
live: Before the sun goes down (Ephesians 4:26)
Settle one quarrel before you sleep tonight, even if it is only with a word.
Go to the vineyard (Matthew 21:29)
Do today the one thing you promised God and have not yet done; if it is confession, go this evening.
2027-02-27.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you sealed us with your Holy Spirit for the day of redemption. Keep us from grieving him with bitterness, anger and slander; let our words give grace to those who hear them, and let the sun never set on our anger. Where we have said yes to you and not gone, and where we have said no, change our minds and send us into your vineyard. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we are made members of one body; before we receive Christ we forgive one another, as God in Christ has forgiven us.

quick: Forty days after his birth, Jesus was presented in the Temple with the offering of the poor.
Simeon took him in his arms: my eyes have seen your salvation.
Anna, who prayed and fasted night and day, spoke of him to all who waited.
2027-02-02.action: Pray by name for a religious sister, brother or priest today and thank them.
2027-02-02.question: Am I waiting for the Lord, or have I stopped expecting him?
catechism: Christ, the end of the law.
kidsaint: Two old friends of God who waited many years in the Temple. When Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus, they knew at once that he was the Saviour! Lesson: God keeps his promises, so we can wait for him with joy.
2027-02-02.special: Mayaltho: the Presentation of the Lord in the Temple. World Day for Consecrated Life.
term: The Syriac name of today's feast, meaning the Entrance: the Lord enters his Temple.

family.explain: When Jesus was forty days old, Mary and Joseph took him to the Temple to give him to God. They were poor, so they brought two little birds. An old man named Simeon took baby Jesus in his arms and said: now I have seen the Saviour!
family.intention: We pray for religious sisters, brothers and priests, especially those from our family and parish.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we give our day to God this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Pala an old man came to the morning Qurbana every day for over forty years, always kneeling in the same place. When his first great-grandson was baptized, the priest placed the baby in his arms for a moment. The old man was silent, and then said softly the words he had prayed for so long: now you are dismissing your servant in peace. His family says that was the happiest they ever saw him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you came to your Temple to meet those who waited for you. Come and meet us now. Amen.
share: They brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord (Luke 2:22). What do I need to present to God?
My eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:30). Where have I seen God's salvation?
She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer (Luke 2:37). How faithful am I in prayer?
pm.resp: Lord, our eyes have seen your salvation.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a light to the nations.
For religious sisters, brothers and priests, on this World Day for Consecrated Life.
For young people discerning a vocation.
For the elderly who pray for the Church, like Simeon and Anna.
For mothers and newborn children.
For our group, that we may be ready to meet the Lord.
pm.close: Father, your Son entered his Temple and was received by those who waited for him. Make us watchful and full of hope, and let his light shine through us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses fasted forty days with God, and his face shone.
God's chosen fast is justice and sharing bread with the hungry.
Jesus overcame the tempter with the word of God: one does not live by bread alone.
2027-02-07.action: At Pethurtha tonight, ask pardon of one family member and forgive one person.
2027-02-07.question: What will make this Great Fast different from last year's?
kidsaint: He stayed on the mountain with God for forty days. When he came down, his face was shining with God's light, and he did not even know it! Lesson: when we spend time with God, his light shines through us.
2027-02-07.special: First Sunday of the Great Fast. Pethurtha. The Great Fast begins tomorrow.
term: The Syriac name of the Great Fast: the fifty days of prayer, fasting and almsgiving before the Pasha of the Lord.

family.explain: Jesus went into the desert and did not eat for forty days. When he was very hungry, the devil said: make bread from these stones! Jesus said no: God's word is more important than bread. In the Great Fast we give up some things to grow closer to God.
family.intention: We pray for a holy Great Fast for our family and our parish.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us give up, and what will we give to the poor, in this Great Fast?”

illus: An illustration

In a family in Kuravilangad the grandmother used to keep a small wooden box on the prayer table during the Great Fast. Every time someone in the house gave up a snack, a tea at the shop or a cinema ticket, the money went into the box. At Easter the children carried it to a home for the elderly nearby. Her grandson, now grown up, says that he forgot most of the sermons of his childhood, but never that box.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, led by the Spirit into the desert, lead us into this Great Fast with you. Amen.
share: He was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights (Exodus 34:28). How will I spend more time with God in these fifty days?
Is not this the fast that I choose? (Isaiah 58:6). What injustice or quarrel must I put right?
One does not live by bread alone (Matthew 4:4). What word of God will I feed on?
pm.resp: Lord, teach us to fast as you fasted.
interc: For the whole Church as she begins the Great Fast.
For those who are tempted and those who have fallen.
For the hungry, the homeless and workers who are oppressed.
For families, that they may be reconciled at Pethurtha.
For our group, that we may put on the new self.
pm.close: Father, your Son overcame the tempter by your word. Strengthen us through these fifty days, and bring us renewed to the joy of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Enoch walked with God in an ordinary home: that is the goal of the fast.
Our Lenten customs are stones that tell our children the story of Christ.
Hear the word and do it: build your house on the rock.
2027-02-14.action: Choose one teaching of Jesus from Matthew 5–7 and live it every day this week.
2027-02-14.question: Am I only hearing the word, or also doing it?
kidsaint: They were two brothers from Thessalonica who went to the Slav peoples. They made an alphabet for their language, so that the people could read the Bible and pray the liturgy in their own words. Lesson: God wants everyone to hear his word and live it!
2027-02-14.special: Second Sunday of the Great Fast.
term: Syriac for the Great Fast: the seven weeks of prayer, fasting and almsgiving that prepare the Church for the Passion and Resurrection of Christ.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about two men who built houses. One built on rock, the other on sand. When the big rain and floods came, the house on sand fell down, but the house on rock stood strong. Jesus says: whoever listens to my words and does them is like the man who built on rock.
family.intention: We pray for families who have lost their homes, and for all who face storms in life.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus says that we can do together this week?”

illus: An illustration

When floodwater rose around a village near Chengannur, an old house built by a grandfather on a high stone plinth stood firm while several newer houses nearby were badly damaged. Long before, the grandfather had insisted on digging down to hard laterite, though the neighbours laughed at the cost and the delay. His grandson, now a catechist, tells his class every Lent: hearing the word is drawing the plan; doing it is the digging. The flood does not ask which house was prettier.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, rock of our salvation, we gather to hear your words. Help us to do them. Amen.
share: Enoch walked with God (Genesis 5:24). What would it mean for me to walk with God this week?
What do these stones mean? (Joshua 4:21). How do I explain my faith to the next generation?
Everyone who hears these words of mine and acts on them (Matthew 7:24). Which word of Jesus am I hearing but not doing?
pm.resp: Lord, build our house on the rock.
interc: For the Church, that she may hear and do the word of God.
For families who have lost their homes in floods and disasters.
For parents and grandparents, that they may hand on the faith.
For catechumens preparing for baptism.
For our group, that our faith may stand in every storm.
pm.close: Father, you call us not only to say Lord, Lord, but to do your will. Build our lives on Christ the rock, and make our families walk with you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Lord shut Noah in: we are saved inside the ark of the Church.
Remove your sandals: bow before you fight; walls fall by prayer.
The Son of Man came to serve and to give his life; drink his cup.
2027-02-21.action: Take on one humble task at home or at work this week that usually falls to someone else.
2027-02-21.question: Am I asking for a seat of honour, or for the grace to drink the Lord's cup and serve?
kidsaint: He was born in Italy and became an orphan when he was very small. As a boy he had to look after pigs, and sometimes he went hungry. Later he studied, became a monk, then a bishop and a cardinal. He called everyone, even popes and bishops, to be honest, humble and to do penance. Lesson: Jesus can make a poor, forgotten child into a great servant of his Church!
2027-02-21.special: Third Sunday of the Great Fast.
term: The Syriac word for cup, used for the chalice of the Holy Qurbana. With the pilasa (paten) it holds the holy mysteries; at Holy Communion we share the cup of which Jesus asked, “Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?”

family.explain: James and John wanted the best seats next to Jesus. Jesus told them: in my kingdom the greatest person is the one who serves others. Jesus himself came to serve us and to give his life for us. At home we can be great like Jesus by helping one another without being asked.
family.intention: We pray for all who serve others quietly: nurses, cleaners, mothers, fathers, the sick and the old.
family.ask: Ask: “Which job at home will each of us do this week to serve the others?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Kanjirappally a newly elected trustee arrived at church early on his first Sunday. The sacristan found him not in the office with the account books but behind the parish hall, cleaning the toilets that the Sunday catechism children would use. The sacristan protested that this was not a trustee's work. The trustee said: the Lord I will be accounting to washed feet. If I start here, I may remember whose money I am counting. The parish still talks about it, though he served only one term.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came not to be served but to serve. Teach us to serve as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: The LORD shut him in (Genesis 7:16). How does the Church keep me safe in the floods of my life?
Remove the sandals from your feet (Joshua 5:15). Where do I need to bow before I fight?
Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? (Matthew 20:22). What cup is the Lord offering me in this season?
pm.resp: Lord, make us servants like you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be an ark of salvation for all peoples.
For those in authority in Church and state, that they may lead by serving.
For all who are struggling against a habit of sin, that the walls may fall.
For persecuted Christians who drink the Lord's cup today.
For our group, that we may seek to serve rather than to be served.
pm.close: Father, your Son came to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many. Keep us in the ark of your Church, rescue us from the body of death, and make us servants of one another. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Babel builds a name for itself and ends in confusion; Pentecost gathers the languages in Christ.
One hidden sin weakened all Israel; the Great Fast is time to search the tent.
The rejected Son has become the cornerstone; we are tenants who owe him fruit.
2027-02-28.action: Do one good work this week that no one will know about.
2027-02-28.question: For whose name am I building, and what fruit am I giving to the Lord of the vineyard?
catechism: Babel and the covenant with Noah.
kidsaint: He was a French priest who died on 28 February 1936. In Paris he cared for hundreds of children who had no family, giving them a home, school and a trade. Lesson: God is a Father to every child, and wants every child to have a home!
2027-02-28.special: Fourth Sunday of the Great Fast.
term: An Aramaic word for Father, used by Jesus in his prayer. By the Spirit of adoption, Christians too call God Abba, with the trust of children.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a man who planted a beautiful vineyard and lent it to some workers. When he sent people to collect the grapes, the workers hurt them. Last of all he sent his own son, and they killed him. Jesus was telling about himself: God sent his Son, and people rejected him. But God raised him up! God has given us good things too, and he asks us to share the fruit.
family.intention: We pray for our parish, the vineyard God has given us.
family.ask: Ask: “What good fruit can our family give to God and to others this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a Syro-Malabar parish in London, a grandmother who came over from Changanassery to look after her grandchildren could not follow their English, and they could not follow her Malayalam. She felt like a stranger in her own family. One evening she began the family prayer anyway, slowly, in Malayalam. Her ten-year-old grandson joined in English, word for word, at the Our Father. Neither understood all of the other's words, but both knew to whom they were speaking. Babel, the parish priest told them later, is healed wherever people say Abba together.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, rejected stone and cornerstone, gather us now as one family before the Father. Amen.
share: Let us make a name for ourselves (Genesis 11:4). Where am I building for my own name?
Israel has sinned; they have taken some of the devoted things (Joshua 7:11). What is hidden in my tent?
All who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God (Romans 8:14). Do I relate to God as a slave or as a child?
The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone (Matthew 21:42). Where do I reject Christ, and where does he hold my life together?
pm.resp: Lord, make us bear the fruits of your kingdom.
interc: For the Church in every language and land, that she may be one.
For migrants and their families, especially those who feel like strangers.
For those carrying hidden sins, that they may find the courage to confess.
For children without families, through the prayers of Blessed Daniel Brottier.
For our parish, that it may give the Lord the fruit he seeks.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to the vineyard of the world, and he was rejected and killed. Raise up in us the fruits of the kingdom, make us your children by the Spirit, and gather us from every tongue into your one Church. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Lord is faithful even when not all have faith.
A woman touched his cloak and was made well: take heart, daughter.
Jesus took the dead girl by the hand and she got up.
2027-02-01.action: Pray by name for one missionary or catechist today.
2027-02-01.question: Do I trust more in my own faith or in the Lord's faithfulness?

family.explain: A sick woman thought: if I only touch Jesus' clothes, I will be well. She touched him and she was healed! Then Jesus went to a house where a little girl had died. He took her hand, and she got up!
family.intention: We pray for sick children and for all who are waiting for healing.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we bring to Jesus today, the way the woman reached out to him?”

illus: An illustration

A nurse at a hospital in Kottayam used to notice an old woman who came every evening to sit beside her husband in the intensive care unit. She said little, but each evening she touched the small crucifix on her rosary and then touched her husband's hand. When the nurse asked her once if she was not tired, she said: my faith is very small, but the Lord is faithful; I only have to reach out.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, faithful and true, we reach out to touch you. Turn to us and heal us. Amen.
share: The Lord is faithful (2 Thessalonians 3:3). Where have I seen his faithfulness in my life?
If I only touch his cloak, I will be made well (Matthew 9:21). What do I want to bring to him?
He took her by the hand, and the girl got up (Matthew 9:25). Whom do I want him to raise up?
pm.resp: Lord, you are faithful; strengthen us.
interc: For the spread of the word of the Lord in our land.
For the sick, especially those suffering for many years.
For parents who grieve for their children.
For those who feel shut out and unclean.
For our group, that our hearts may be directed to the love of God.
pm.close: Father, your Son turned to the woman who reached out and raised the girl who had died. Strengthen our faith and guard us from the evil one. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: proclaim the message, whether the time is favourable or unfavourable.
The Samaritan woman left her water jar and brought her town to Jesus.
Jesus: my food is to do the will of him who sent me.
2027-02-03.action: Thank God today by name for the person who first taught you the faith.
2027-02-03.question: What feeds me more: my own wishes or the will of God?

family.explain: A woman met Jesus at a well. She was so happy that she forgot her water jar and ran into town shouting: come and see! Many people came to meet Jesus because of her.
family.intention: We pray for catechism teachers and all who teach the faith to children.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught us about Jesus, and how can we thank them?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in a parish near Thodupuzha taught the Sunday class for nearly forty years. Many of her pupils drifted away, and she sometimes wondered if her work had borne any fruit. In her old age one of those pupils, now a priest, came back to celebrate a Holy Qurbana in the parish. In his homily he said: she sowed, and I am only reaping. She sat in the front row, crying.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the living water. Fill us, so that we too may leave our jars and run to tell others. Amen.
share: Proclaim the message; be persistent whether the time is favorable or unfavorable (2 Timothy 4:2). Where am I called to speak about Christ?
She left her water jar (John 4:28). What must I leave to follow Jesus?
My food is to do the will of him who sent me (John 4:34). What is God's will for me this week?
pm.resp: Lord, may your will be our food.
interc: For preachers, catechists and missionaries.
For those who have itching ears and turn away from the truth.
For outsiders who are waiting to hear about Christ.
For those who first taught us the faith, living and departed.
For our group, that we may do the Father's will.
pm.close: Father, your Son found his food in doing your will. Send us into the harvest and give us joy in the work. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter: regard the patience of our Lord as salvation.
Jesus: do not judge; first take the log out of your own eye.
St John de Britto became all things to all people and died for Christ in Tamil Nadu.
2027-02-04.action: Before criticizing anyone today, name one fault of your own and ask God's pardon.
2027-02-04.question: Do I measure others with the patience God shows me?

family.explain: Jesus told a funny picture-story: a man with a big log in his own eye tries to take a tiny speck out of his friend's eye! Jesus means: before we find fault with others, let us look at our own faults.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, through St John de Britto.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we go one whole day this week without finding fault with anyone?”

illus: An illustration

A Syro-Malabar family from Kerala, working in Chennai, visited the shrine of St John de Britto at Oriyur. The father, who was quick to criticize his Tamil neighbours, read on a board how Arul Anandar had learned their language, worn their dress and eaten their food in order to love them. On the way home he said quietly: I have lived among them ten years and never learned to greet them in their own tongue. The next week he began to learn Tamil from the neighbour's son.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, merciful and patient, take the logs from our eyes so that we may see clearly. Amen.
share: Regard the patience of our Lord as salvation (2 Peter 3:15). How has God been patient with me?
Do not judge, and you will not be judged (Luke 6:37). Whom have I been judging?
I have become all things to all people (1 Corinthians 9:22). Whom do I need to understand better?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us, as we have mercy on others.
interc: For the Church, that she may be patient and merciful.
For missionaries who live among other cultures, through St John de Britto.
For those we have judged harshly.
For the Church in Tamil Nadu.
For our group, that we may forgive and give in good measure.
pm.close: Father, you are patient with us and want all to be saved. Make us merciful as you are merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ezekiel saw dry bones rise to life when God's breath entered them.
What is sown in weakness is raised in power: we believe in the resurrection of the body.
Praying for the dead is a work of mercy; the Holy Qurbana is the greatest help we can give them.
2027-02-05.action: Pray by name today for each of your departed family members.
2027-02-05.question: Do I remember my dead before God, or only in memory?

family.explain: God showed the prophet Ezekiel a valley full of dry bones. When God breathed on them, they came to life and stood up! God promises that he will raise our dear ones who have died, and give them new life.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all our family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we make a list of our family members who have died and pray for them together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Changanassery the young people of the family union noticed some old graves in the cemetery that no one visited any more; the families had moved away or died out. On the Friday of the Faithful Departed they cleaned those graves, lit candles on them, and asked the parish priest to pray the oppees there too. An old woman watching said: now no one in this cemetery is forgotten.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, we gather in communion with all who have gone before us. Breathe your Spirit upon us and upon them. Amen.
share: Mortal, can these bones live? (Ezekiel 37:3). Is there anything in me that feels dry and dead?
Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lives on (Sirach 44:14). Whom do I remember before God?
Just as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me (Matthew 25:40). Whom have I served, and whom have I passed by?
pm.resp: Eternal rest grant to them, O Lord.
interc: For all the faithful departed, especially our families and benefactors.
For those who have no one to pray for them.
For those who are dying today.
For the grieving and the lonely.
For our group, that we may serve Christ in the least.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the first fruits of those who have died. Grant eternal rest to all the departed, and bring us all together into your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Laodiceans were lukewarm and said: we need nothing.
Christ stands at the door and knocks; if we open, he will come in and eat with us.
The crowds laid their sick at Jesus' feet, and he cured them.
2027-02-06.action: Make or plan a good confession before the Great Fast begins.
2027-02-06.question: Is there any area where I say to God: I need nothing?
