family.explain: Jesus says: I am standing at your door, knocking. If you open, I will come in and eat with you! Many people brought sick friends to Jesus, and he healed them all.
family.intention: We pray for the sick, and for a good beginning of the Great Fast.
family.ask: Ask: “What will our family do for Jesus in this Great Fast?”

illus: An illustration

A young professional in Kochi, successful and busy, went to the Holy Qurbana only at Christmas and Easter. When a friend asked if he prayed, he laughed: I have everything I need. A few months later his company closed and his father fell ill in the same week. Sitting late at night in the hospital corridor, he found himself reading the words on a picture on the wall: I am standing at the door, knocking. He said later: I had kept the door locked because I thought I was rich. That night I opened it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you stand at the door and knock. We open the door to you; come in and stay with us. Amen.
share: Because you are lukewarm, I am about to spit you out of my mouth (Revelation 3:16). Where am I lukewarm?
If you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in (Revelation 3:20). What keeps my door closed?
They put them at his feet, and he cured them (Matthew 15:30). Whom will I bring to Jesus' feet?
pm.resp: Lord, come in and stay with us.
interc: For the whole Church, that the Great Fast may be a time of true conversion.
For those who are lukewarm or have drifted away.
For the sick and the disabled.
For those who think they need nothing.
For our group, that we may open the door to Christ.
pm.close: Father, your Son knocks at our door and heals all who are laid at his feet. Prepare us for the Great Fast with humble and open hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Great Fast begins: we are dust, and God is our life.
God says again, “Let there be light”; the fast is a new creation.
First be reconciled, then offer your gift.
2027-02-08.action: Take the first step of reconciliation with one person today.
2027-02-08.question: Who has something against me, and what is my first step?

family.explain: Jesus says: if you come to church with a gift for God and remember that your brother is upset with you, leave the gift, go and make peace first, and then come back. God wants our hearts at peace with one another before we pray together.
family.intention: We pray for families where people are not speaking to one another.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family to whom we need to say sorry today?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers near Pala had not spoken for six years because of a boundary wall between their plots. On the morning of the Vibhoodi the younger one stood in the line for the ashes and found himself just behind his elder brother. When the priest said the words about dust, he thought: our wall will outlast both of us. After the service he walked over and said only, come home for tea. The wall is still there, but the gate in it is open now.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we begin the Great Fast before you. Make us dust that is open to your breath. Amen.
share: Let there be light (Genesis 1:3). Where do I need God's light this Lent?
Be strong and courageous (Joshua 1:9). What crossing lies before me in these seven weeks?
First be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). With whom must I make peace?
pm.resp: Lord, create a new heart in us.
interc: For the whole Church as she begins the Great Fast.
For all who are estranged from their families.
For the poor, who will receive what our fast saves.
For those who find fasting difficult because of illness or age.
For our group, that we may keep this fast with joy.
pm.close: Father, you call us back to you with fasting and prayer. Reconcile us with you and with one another, and lead us through these days to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God made us from dust and breathed his life into us.
God's kindness is meant to lead us to repentance.
Jesus asks us to walk the second mile.
2027-02-09.action: Put aside today the money your fast saves, in a box for the poor.
2027-02-09.question: Do I take God's kindness for granted?

family.explain: Jesus says: if someone is unkind to you, do not hit back. If someone asks you to walk one mile with him, walk two! Jesus wants us to be more generous than anyone expects, because God is so generous with us.
family.intention: We pray for people who have hurt us.
family.ask: Ask: “What extra kindness can each of us do this week?”

illus: An illustration

An autorickshaw driver in Kochi was asked by an elderly passenger to wait while she collected her medicines, though she said she had no money to pay for the waiting. He waited, and then carried her bags up three flights of stairs. She asked his name so that she could pray for him. He smiled and said: it is the Great Fast, Ammachi; this is my second mile.

pm.open: Lord God, you formed us from the dust and gave us your breath. Breathe on us now as we pray. Amen.
share: The Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7). What does it mean for me that I carry God's breath?
God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance (Romans 2:4). How has God's kindness called me back?
Go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). Where is God asking me to give more?
pm.resp: Lord, make us generous like you.
interc: For the Church, that she may show God's kindness to all.
For those who judge others harshly, and for those who are judged.
For the poor who depend on our generosity this Lent.
For those who have hurt us, and those we have hurt.
For our group, that we may walk the second mile together.
pm.close: Father, your kindness leads us to repentance. Make our fasting generous and our hearts patient, like your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: It is not good to be alone: we keep the fast as families.
Rahab believed and was saved; be a doer of the word.
Pray in secret; the Father sees and knows what you need.
2027-02-10.action: Pray for ten minutes today in a quiet room with the door shut.
2027-02-10.question: Do I pray to be seen, or to be with the Father?

family.explain: Jesus says: when you pray, you do not need to show off or use lots of words. Go to a quiet place, shut the door, and talk to your Father in heaven. He already knows what you need, and he loves to hear you!
family.intention: We pray for married couples and for families keeping the Great Fast together.
family.ask: Ask: “Where in our home can we make a quiet corner for prayer?”

illus: An illustration

A young couple in Kottayam, both working long shifts, agreed at the start of the Great Fast to switch off their phones at nine each night and pray together for ten minutes. The first evenings were awkward; the silence felt long. By Easter the wife said they had talked to each other more in those seven weeks than in the whole year before. The husband said: we went into the room to talk to God, and we found each other there too.

pm.open: Father in heaven, we have come into your presence. You see in secret and you know what we need. Hear us. Amen.
share: It is not good that the man should be alone (Genesis 2:18). How can my family keep this fast together?
The LORD your God is indeed God in heaven above and on earth below (Joshua 2:11). What does Rahab's faith teach me?
Pray to your Father who is in secret (Matthew 6:6). Do I have an inner room for prayer?
pm.resp: Father, teach us to pray.
interc: For the Church in Kerala, of every tradition, walking through the Lenten season together.
For married couples, that they may pray together.
For those who are lonely, especially the elderly living alone.
For those who have never learned to pray.
For our group, that our prayer may be sincere.
pm.close: Father, you see in secret and know our needs before we ask. Draw us into prayer that is honest and simple, and bless our families in this holy fast. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Sin began with suspicion; God still asks: where are you?
God goes before us like the ark into the river.
Strive first for the kingdom; the Father knows what you need.
2027-02-11.action: Write down your biggest worry and hand it to God in prayer.
2027-02-11.question: Where am I hiding from God?

family.explain: Jesus says: look at the birds. They do not have kitchens or shops, but God feeds them. Look at the flowers. They do not sew clothes, but God makes them beautiful. You are worth much more to God than birds and flowers! So do not worry. Put God first.
family.intention: We pray for sick people and for those who care for them.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we are worried about? Let us give it to God together.”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Thodupuzha lay awake every night worrying about her son working in the Gulf. At the start of the Great Fast she began a small practice: each night she wrote her worry on a slip of paper and dropped it into a box placed before the image of Our Lady. By Easter the box was full. She laughed and told her neighbour: I gave the box the night shift. My son still has problems, but now I sleep, and I pray better in the morning.

pm.open: Lord God, you call us by name: where are you? Here we are, Lord. Amen.
share: Where are you? (Genesis 3:9). Where am I hiding from God?
Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you (Joshua 3:5). How am I preparing for what God wants to do?
Strive first for the kingdom of God (Matthew 6:33). What comes first in my life?
pm.resp: Lord, we trust in your care.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's providence.
For the sick, through the prayers of Our Lady of Lourdes.
For doctors, nurses and caregivers.
For those overwhelmed by worry about money, work or children.
For our group, that we may seek first the kingdom.
pm.close: Father, you feed the birds and clothe the lilies. Free us from anxiety, forgive our hiding, and teach us to seek your kingdom first. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God asks: where is your brother? We are our brothers' keepers.
Abraham hoped against hope and believed God's promise.
First take the log out of your own eye.
2027-02-12.action: Walk the Way of the Cross today, at church or at home.
2027-02-12.question: Whom do I judge, and what is the log in my own eye?

family.explain: Cain was jealous of his brother Abel and hurt him very badly. God asked Cain: where is your brother? Cain said: I do not know; am I my brother's keeper? But God wants us to look after one another. Every brother and sister is a gift from God.
family.intention: We pray for brothers and sisters who are quarrelling.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we look after each other better in our family?”

illus: An illustration

A man in Alappuzha used to criticise his neighbour's drinking at every parish gathering. One Lenten Friday, at the station where Jesus falls the third time, he suddenly remembered his own temper at home, and how his children went quiet when he came in. That evening he went to his neighbour's house, not to preach, but to ask him to walk the Way of the Cross with him the next Friday. The neighbour came. Both of them, the man said later, had logs to carry.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this Friday of the Great Fast we stand before your Cross. Look on us with mercy. Amen.
share: Where is your brother Abel? (Genesis 4:9). Whom am I neglecting?
Hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). Where do I need Abraham's faith?
First take the log out of your own eye (Matthew 7:5). What do I need to see in myself?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church as she walks the Way of the Cross this Friday.
For victims of violence and for those who have killed.
For brothers and sisters divided by jealousy or property.
For those who have lost hope.
For our group, that we may stop judging one another.
pm.close: Father, the blood of your Son speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. Make us keepers of one another and give us the faith of Abraham. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: All have sinned; we are justified by grace as a gift.
The Our Father is the programme of the Great Fast.
The forgiven must forgive.
2027-02-13.action: Pray the Our Father slowly, a minute on each line.
2027-02-13.question: Do I fast with gratitude or with pride?

family.explain: Jesus taught his friends a prayer: the Our Father. We call God our Father, we ask him for our bread each day, and we ask him to forgive us, just as we forgive others. Jesus says this is very important: if we forgive, God forgives us.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who finds it hard to forgive.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we pray the Our Father together slowly tonight, and think about each line?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in Irinjalakuda asked her class to pray the Our Father aloud, pausing after the words about forgiving others. One boy fell silent at that line. Afterwards he told her he could not say it, because he was angry with his cousin. The next Sunday he came early and whispered: we made up yesterday. Now I can say the whole prayer.

pm.open: Our Father in heaven, we come to you as your children, justified by your grace. Hallowed be your name. Amen.
share: They are now justified by his grace as a gift (Romans 3:24). Do I receive God's love as a gift, or try to earn it?
Give us this day our daily bread (Matthew 6:11). What does fasting teach me about this petition?
If you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). Whom must I forgive?
pm.resp: Father, forgive us as we forgive.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the free gift of God's grace.
For those who carry old wounds and cannot forgive.
For those who have no daily bread.
For those in the time of trial and temptation.
For our group, that we may pray the Our Father with sincere hearts.
pm.close: Father, you justify us freely in your Son. Teach us to pray as he taught us, and to forgive as we have been forgiven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We fast from clean food so that the heart may become clean.
What defiles comes from within; guard the heart.
God saved us by his mercy, through the water of rebirth and the Spirit.
2027-02-15.action: Speak evil of no one today, and say one kind word about someone you usually criticise.
2027-02-15.question: What comes out of my heart when I am tired or hurt?

family.explain: Jesus says that dirt on our hands or food in our stomach does not make us bad. What makes us bad comes from inside: angry thoughts, lies, jealousy, unkind words. During the Great Fast we give up some food, but we also ask Jesus to clean our hearts.
family.intention: We pray that our home may be free of unkind words this week.
family.ask: Ask: “Which unkind word shall we all try not to say at home this week?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother near Thrissur was known in her parish for the strictness of her Lenten fast: no fish, no eggs, no milk in her tea for fifty days. One Lent her granddaughter, home from college, asked her gently why she still complained about the daughter-in-law every evening. The old woman was silent for a long time. That year she added one more thing to her fast: no complaint about anyone at the dinner table. Her son said later that it was the hardest fast she ever kept, and the first one the whole house noticed.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you look into our hearts. Clean them by your Spirit as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: Nothing outside a person can defile (Mark 7:15). What does my fast this year really aim at?
From within, from the human heart (Mark 7:21). Which of the things Jesus lists do I struggle with most?
Speak evil of no one (Titus 3:2). Where does my tongue most need a fast?
pm.resp: Lord, create in us a clean heart.
interc: For the Church, that her fasting may bear the fruit of clean hearts.
For families where harsh words have become a habit.
For those who are victims of slander and gossip.
For the newly baptised and for catechumens.
For our group, that our words may build one another up.
pm.close: Father, by the goodness and loving kindness of our Saviour you have washed us and renewed us. Keep our hearts clean, our tongues gentle and our fast sincere. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Creation groans like a mother in labour; glory is coming.
We are saved in hope and wait with patience.
Ask, search, knock: the Father never gives a stone for bread.
2027-02-16.action: Bring one intention to God today and promise to keep asking until Easter.
2027-02-16.question: Do I pray like a child who trusts the Father, or like a stranger who expects to be refused?

family.explain: Jesus says: if a child asks his father for bread, the father will not give him a stone. God is a much better Father than any father on earth. He hears us when we ask. Sometimes he gives exactly what we ask, sometimes something better, but always what is good for us.
family.intention: We pray for children who are hungry and have no one to give them bread.
family.ask: Ask: “What shall we ask God for together, every day until Easter?”

illus: An illustration

A boy in Muvattupuzha begged his father all one summer for a ride on the new motorbike out on the highway. The father kept saying no, and every evening took him instead for a long walk to the river, where they talked about school and friends. The boy sulked for weeks. Twenty years later, at his father's funeral, he told the parish that those evening walks were the best gift his father ever gave him. He had asked for speed; his father gave him time.

pm.open: Heavenly Father, we come to you as children. We ask, we search, we knock. Open to us. Amen.
share: Creation waits with eager longing (Romans 8:19). Where do I see the world groaning around me?
In hope we were saved (Romans 8:24). What helps me to wait with patience?
Ask, and it will be given you (Matthew 7:7). What have I stopped asking God for, and why?
pm.resp: Father, give good things to those who ask you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a people of hope.
For farmers and families facing water shortage in the summer months.
For those who have stopped praying because they feel unheard.
For all who are making a Lenten retreat these weeks.
For our group, that we may do to others as we would have them do to us.
pm.close: Father, you hear the groaning of your creation and the prayers of your children. Fill us with hope, teach us to ask with confidence, and make us generous to everyone. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus saw the faith of those who carried the paralysed man.
He healed the deepest paralysis first: your sins are forgiven.
God has given human beings authority to forgive in Christ's name.
2027-02-17.action: Carry someone to Christ today: a visit, a phone call, an offer of a ride to church.
2027-02-17.question: Am I being carried, or am I carrying someone, or am I standing at a distance?

family.explain: Some friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus. Jesus saw how much they believed, and he said to the man: your sins are forgiven. Then he said: stand up and walk home. Jesus can heal our bodies, and even more, he can heal our hearts. In confession he still says to us: your sins are forgiven.
family.intention: We pray for the sick and elderly people in our parish who cannot come to church.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we could visit or help to come to church this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Changanassery an old man who had been paralysed by a stroke had not been to church for three years. During the Great Fast four young men from the parish youth group asked whether they might bring him to the penitential service. They carried him down the steep path from his house in a plastic chair, two on each side, and up the church steps. After his confession he wept, and then he laughed, and said he had not felt so light for years. One of the four said afterwards that they had only carried a chair; the Lord had carried the man.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we come to you carried by one another's faith. Speak your word of pardon over us. Amen.
share: When Jesus saw their faith (Matthew 9:2). Whose faith has carried me in my life?
Your sins are forgiven (Matthew 9:2). What keeps me from the sacrament of reconciliation?
Present your members as slaves to righteousness (Romans 6:19). How can my hands and tongue serve holiness this week?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us and heal us.
interc: For priests, that they may be generous ministers of God's forgiveness this Lent.
For the sick, the paralysed and the housebound.
For young people who serve the elderly and the sick in our parishes.
For those who have stayed away from confession for many years.
For our group, that we may carry one another to Christ.
pm.close: Father, you have given such authority to human beings that sins are forgiven in the name of your Son. Make us a people who carry one another, and raise us to walk in newness of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Our faithlessness does not cancel God's faithfulness.
We may never do evil so that good may come.
Let your yes be yes and your no be no.
2027-02-18.action: Speak without a single oath today, and keep one promise you have neglected.
2027-02-18.question: Is my plain word trusted at home and at work?

family.explain: Jesus says we do not need to say “I promise on God” or “by my mother” to make people believe us. If we always tell the truth, our yes will be enough. God always keeps his word, and he wants his children to keep theirs.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who finds it hard to tell the truth.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a promise one of us made that we have not kept yet?”

illus: An illustration

A shopkeeper in Kunnamkulam had a habit of adding “daivathaane” to every price and every promise of delivery. One Great Fast a young customer, half joking, asked him why God had to be brought into the price of rice. The question stayed with him. He decided to stop swearing for the whole of Lent, and found he also had to stop exaggerating, because without the oath the exaggeration sounded empty. Years later his customers say they never bargain with him. They say: when he says it is the last price, it is.

pm.open: Faithful God, your word is true for ever. Make our words true as we pray together. Amen.
share: Will their faithlessness nullify the faithfulness of God? (Romans 3:3). When have I experienced God's faithfulness after my own failure?
Let us do evil so that good may come? (Romans 3:8). Where am I tempted to justify a small wrong for a good end?
Let your word be Yes, Yes or No, No (Matthew 5:37). Where does my speech need more simplicity and truth?
pm.resp: Lord, make our yes a yes and our no a no.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a witness to truth in the world.
For those who give evidence in courts and for all judges and lawyers.
For families broken by lies and broken promises.
For people in business and public life, that they may be honest.
For our group, that our words may be simple and true.
pm.close: Father, your faithfulness is great and your mercies are new every morning. Make us truthful in word and faithful in deed, like your Son, in whom every promise of yours is yes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Sin grieves the heart of God; the Cross shows how deeply.
At Gilgal God rolled away the disgrace of Egypt; he can roll away ours.
Do not hide behind “we do not know”; say what you know and change.
2027-02-19.action: Make the Way of the Cross today and name one sin plainly before the Lord.
2027-02-19.question: Where am I saying “I do not know” when in fact I know and do not want to change?

family.explain: The Bible says that when people became very wicked, God was sad in his heart. Sin is not just breaking a rule; it makes God sad, the way it makes our parents sad when we hurt each other. But Noah loved God and walked with him, and God was pleased with him. On Fridays of the Great Fast we remember how much Jesus suffered for our sins.
family.intention: We pray for all who suffer because of violence in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do today to make God's heart glad?”

illus: An illustration

A software engineer from Angamaly, home on leave, climbed the hill of Malayattoor one Lenten night with his father, who insisted on going barefoot. Halfway up the son asked, a little impatiently, why they could not take it easy like the families resting on the rocks. The father said: I am carrying something up this hill that I want to leave there. At the top he went to confession in the queue near the chapel. Coming down at dawn he walked so lightly that the son had to hurry to keep up.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, crucified for us, we gather on this Friday of the fast. Roll away our disgrace and heal us. Amen.
share: It grieved him to his heart (Genesis 6:6). How does it change me to see my sin as grieving God?
Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt (Joshua 5:9). What disgrace do I want the Lord to roll away?
We do not know (Mark 11:33). Where am I evading a truth I already know?
pm.resp: Lord, by your holy Cross, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the mercy of the Cross.
For places filled with violence, as in the days of Noah.
For pilgrims climbing Malayattoor and all our hill shrines this Lent.
For those who carry a hidden shame and dare not speak of it.
For our group, that we may be honest before God.
pm.close: Father, your heart grieves over our sins, yet you sent your Son to bear them on the Cross. Roll away our disgrace, feed us on our journey, and make us honest and humble before you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Some would neither dance nor mourn: the problem was the heart, not the music.
There is a time to fast and a time to feast; let us do each fully.
Judge yourself before you judge others; let your deeds show wisdom.
2027-02-20.action: Give up one harmful habit for the rest of the fast and give the saving to the poor.
2027-02-20.question: Am I responding to what God is asking of me in this season, or finding excuses?

family.explain: Jesus tells about children who would not join any game: not the happy wedding game, not the sad funeral game. Some people were like that with God. They found fault with John for fasting and with Jesus for eating with sinners. Jesus wants us to respond to God with our whole heart: sad for our sins now, and full of joy at Easter.
family.intention: We pray for families hurt by alcohol and other addictions.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we complain about instead of doing what God asks?”

illus: An illustration

A fisherman in Chellanam took the Lenten pledge to give up drinking. His friends at the evening gathering laughed and said he had become a priest. When Easter came he bought new clothes for his children with the money he had saved and invited the same friends home for appam and stew. One of them, half embarrassed, said: now you are celebrating too much. His wife laughed and said: first you said he does not drink with you, now you say he eats too much with you. Then she served them a second helping.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, friend of sinners, we come to you with open hearts. Help us to respond to your call. Amen.
share: We played the flute for you, and you did not dance (Matthew 11:17). Where have I failed to respond to God's call?
Is it not those who are inside that you are to judge? (1 Corinthians 5:12). What in my own life needs honest judgment this Lent?
Wisdom is vindicated by her deeds (Matthew 11:19). What fruit should my fast bear?
pm.resp: Lord, give us hearts that respond to you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be holy within and patient with all.
For men and women struggling with alcohol and drug addiction, and for their families.
For those who mock faith, that they may come to know Christ.
For all who have taken a Lenten pledge, that they may persevere.
For our group, that our deeds may show the wisdom of God.
pm.close: Father, your wisdom is shown in the deeds of those who follow your Son. Give us sorrow for sin in this fast, joy in the Resurrection, and strength to persevere. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: we serve in the new life of the Spirit, not under the old written code.
Jesus: love God with all your heart, and your neighbour as yourself.
Not far from the kingdom is not yet inside it.
2027-02-22.action: Let the first commandment decide one concrete choice today.
2027-02-22.question: Is my fast a set of rules, or an act of love?

family.explain: A teacher asked Jesus which rule was the most important of all. Jesus said: love God with your whole heart, and love your neighbour as much as you love yourself. All the other rules are there to help us do these two things.
family.intention: We pray for those who are attending Lenten retreats this week.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way each of us can love God, and one way we can love a neighbour, before tomorrow?”

illus: An illustration

For thirty years a man in Kottayam drove his wife to church every Sunday and waited in the car outside, reading the newspaper. He knew the prayers and could argue theology with the parish priest. On the second evening of the parish Lenten retreat a heavy rain came down, and he ran inside to take shelter at the back. He heard a preacher say: you can know every answer and still be standing outside. The next evening he came in without the rain.

pm.open: Lord, you have set us free in the new life of the Spirit. Teach us to love with our whole heart. Amen.
share: The new life of the Spirit (Romans 7:6). Where has my faith become only a set of rules?
With all your heart (Mark 12:30). What part of my heart have I kept back from God?
You are not far from the kingdom of God (Mark 12:34). What step would bring me inside?
pm.resp: Lord, teach us to love.
interc: For the Church, that her laws may always serve love.
For all who are preaching and attending Lenten retreats.
For those who stand at the door of the Church and do not come in.
For the Pope, successor of Peter.
For our group, that we may love God and one another with our whole heart.
pm.close: Father, you ask of us one thing: to love you and our neighbour. Pour out your Spirit on us, so that our fast may be a gift of love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Israel's story in the desert was written down to instruct us.
God is faithful: no testing beyond our strength, and always a way out.
Be alert at all times and pray, so that the heart is not weighed down.
2027-02-23.action: Name what weighs your heart down most, and take one step against it today.
2027-02-23.question: Where am I sure that I am standing, and so in danger of falling?

family.explain: Jesus says: be careful that your heart does not become heavy with too many treats, too much worry, or wrong things. Stay awake inside, like a watchman, and keep praying, so that you are always ready to meet Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family or parish who is struggling with drinking or with worry.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes our hearts heavy at home, and what can we give up together this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer in Bengaluru promised his mother at Pethurtha that he would not drink during the Great Fast. In the third week his office team held a farewell party, and the bottles came round the table. He felt the old pull and the teasing of his friends. He went out to the balcony, phoned his mother, and asked her simply to pray the Hail Mary with him. Then he went back in and ordered lime juice. Later he said: the way out was a phone call long.

pm.open: Lord, you are faithful. Keep us awake and watchful in prayer. Amen.
share: They were written down to instruct us (1 Corinthians 10:11). What does Israel's grumbling in the desert teach me?
God is faithful (1 Corinthians 10:13). When has God shown me a way out of temptation?
Be alert at all times, praying (Luke 21:36). What makes my heart heavy and sleepy?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us watchful.
interc: For the Church, that she may stay awake and ready for the Lord.
For all who are struggling with alcohol or other addictions, and for their families.
For those weighed down by worries about money, work or health.
For persecuted Christians, through the prayers of St Polycarp.
For our group, that we may stand firm to the end.
pm.close: Faithful Father, you do not let us be tested beyond our strength. Keep us watchful in prayer and make us stand before your Son with joy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter: do not repay evil for evil, but repay with a blessing.
Jesus: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.
God's sun and rain fall on everyone; our love must leave no one out.
2027-02-24.action: Pray by name today for one person who has hurt you.
2027-02-24.question: Whom have I left out of my love and my prayer?

family.explain: Jesus says: it is easy to love people who love us. But God wants us to love even people who are unkind to us, and to pray for them. God sends the sunshine and the rain on everyone, good and bad. We are his children when we love like that.
family.intention: We pray for someone who has been unkind to one of us.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school, at work or in the neighbourhood we find hard to like? Let us pray for them together now.”

illus: An illustration

A nurse from Thodupuzha working in a Gulf hospital had a supervisor who seemed to find fault with everything she did. During the Great Fast she wrote the supervisor's name on a slip of paper, kept it in her prayer book, and prayed for her every night. Nothing changed for weeks. Then, in Holy Week, the supervisor stopped her in the corridor, her eyes red, and said: my mother is very ill at home; I know you pray; will you pray for her? The nurse said: I have been praying for you for forty days already.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you prayed for your enemies. Soften our hearts as we pray now. Amen.
share: Repay with a blessing (1 Peter 3:9). Where am I caught in the circle of returning evil?
Seek peace and pursue it (1 Peter 3:11). What peace do I need to run after?
Love your enemies (Matthew 5:44). Whose name do I find hardest to say in prayer?
pm.resp: Lord, make our love whole.
interc: For the Church, that she may answer hatred with blessing.
For those who persecute Christians, that they may come to know Christ.
For families divided by quarrels over property and inheritance.
For those who have hurt us, and those we have hurt.
For our group, that we may be children of our Father in heaven.
pm.close: Father, you make your sun rise on the evil and on the good. Make us perfect as you are perfect, loving without exception. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: serve as to the Lord, for we all have one Master in heaven.
Jesus warns against religion for show that devours widows' houses.
Blessed Rani Maria served the poor at Udainagar and died for Christ in 1995; her family forgave her killer.
2027-02-25.action: Offer your work to Christ before you begin it today.
2027-02-25.question: Do I serve for the Lord, or for the honour of being seen?

family.explain: Paul tells children to obey their parents and to honour their father and mother. He also tells fathers and mothers not to make their children angry, but to bring them up gently in the ways of the Lord. A Christian home is a place where everyone serves one another for Jesus' sake.
family.intention: We pray for the Clarist sisters and all who work among the poor in North India, through Blessed Rani Maria.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us serve someone in our family today, as if we were serving Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A parish youth group from Ernakulam travelled by train to Udainagar to pray at the tomb of Blessed Rani Maria. They had expected a grand shrine and found a simple place among small villages. An old tribal woman, seeing them, held up her hands and said through an interpreter: sister taught me to write my name; before that I put my thumb on the moneylender's paper. One of the young men said afterwards: I came to see a martyr, and I found out what she died for.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are our one Master. Teach us to serve as you served. Amen.
share: As to the Lord (Ephesians 6:7). Whom am I really trying to please in my daily work?
They devour widows' houses (Mark 12:40). Where do I see the poor being exploited, and what can I do?
Sheep into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16). What courage does Blessed Rani Maria ask of me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us your servants.
interc: For the Church, that she may serve the poor without seeking honour.
For the Franciscan Clarist sisters and all missionaries in North India, through Blessed Rani Maria.
For poor families trapped by debt and moneylenders.
For prisoners, that like Samundar Singh they may find repentance and new life.
For our group, that we may forgive as Rani Maria's family forgave.
pm.close: Father, your servant Rani Maria served the poor and gave her life for your Son. Through her prayers make us faithful in service, brave among wolves and generous in forgiveness. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God hangs his bow in the clouds and promises to remember his covenant.
Jericho falls through patient obedience; Lenten prayer is often slow and repeated.
No condemnation in Christ; God is the God of the living.
2027-02-26.action: Pray the Way of the Cross today in silence, and name your departed at the end.
2027-02-26.question: Do I still live under condemnation, when Christ has set me free?

family.explain: After the great flood God made a promise to Noah and to every animal: never again will a flood destroy the earth. God put a rainbow in the sky as a sign. When we see a rainbow, we can remember that God always keeps his promises.
family.intention: We pray for our family members who have died, that they may live with God.
family.ask: Ask: “What promise of God shall we thank him for tonight?”

illus: An illustration

After the Way of the Cross on a Lenten Friday, a grandmother in Kuravilangad took her small grandson to the cemetery to light a candle at her husband's grave. The boy asked: is Appachan dead? She thought for a while and said: his body is sleeping here, but Jesus says God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. That is why we bring a light and not only flowers. The boy carefully shielded the flame from the wind all the way to the grave.

pm.open: Lord God, you remember your covenant for ever. Remember us now as we pray. Amen.
share: I will remember my covenant (Genesis 9:15). When has God been faithful to me though I was not faithful to him?
You shall not shout until the day I tell you (Joshua 6:10). Can I keep praying even when nothing seems to change?
He is God not of the dead, but of the living (Mark 12:27). How does this change the way I remember my departed?
pm.resp: Lord, remember us in your kingdom.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim that in Christ there is no condemnation.
For those who carry the burden of guilt and cannot believe they are forgiven.
For pilgrims climbing Malayattoor and all who keep the Way of the Cross.
For our departed relatives and friends.
For our group, that we may set our minds on the Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful to your covenant and the God of the living. Free us from condemnation, keep us patient in prayer, and raise us up with all our dead. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: do not let the sun go down on your anger.
Let your words give grace to those who hear.
The son who said no but went did the will of his father.
2027-02-27.action: Settle one quarrel before you sleep tonight.
2027-02-27.question: Where have I said yes to God and not gone?

family.explain: A father asked his two sons to help in the vineyard. One said no, but later he felt sorry and went to work. The other said yes, but never went! Jesus asks: which son really obeyed? It is not enough to say yes to God; we must also do it. And if we have said no, we can always change our minds.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family who is angry or hurt tonight.
family.ask: Ask: “Before we go to sleep, is there anyone we need to make peace with?”

illus: An illustration

When a rubber farmer near Kanjirappally fell ill, he asked his son, home from college, to do the morning tapping. The boy said: I cannot, Appa, I have exams, and I am not getting up at four. His father said nothing. The next morning the mother woke before dawn and saw a small headlamp moving among the rubber trees. At breakfast no one mentioned it. But that evening, after the night prayer, when the son came for the blessing, the father held his hand a little longer than usual.

pm.open: Lord, you sealed us with your Spirit. Guard our tongues and soften our hearts as we pray. Amen.
share: Do not let the sun go down on your anger (Ephesians 4:26). What anger have I carried for more than a day?
So that your words may give grace (Ephesians 4:29). Whose day have I made heavier by my words?
Later he changed his mind and went (Matthew 21:29). What no can I turn into a yes this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us kind and tenderhearted.
interc: For the Church, that her words may always give grace.
For families where anger is carried from day to day.
For those preparing for confession this evening.
For those who have said no to God for many years.
For our group, that we may forgive as God in Christ has forgiven us.
pm.close: Father, you are patient with sons who say no and with sons who say yes and do not go. Change our minds, send us into your vineyard, and make us kind to one another. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the Lord enters his Temple. Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, as the law commanded, and they offer a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons (Luke 2:24). It was the offering of the poor.

The law of Leviticus said that a mother who could not afford a lamb could bring two birds. But on that day the true Lamb was in his mother's arms. The poor offering was made for the One who would offer himself for the whole world.

Simeon, righteous and devout, has waited all his life. Guided by the Spirit he comes into the Temple, takes the child in his arms and says: master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:29–30).

Then he tells Mary that this child will be a sign that will be opposed, and that a sword will pierce her soul. Paul, in the Epistle, grieves that many stumbled over this stone. Yet Christ is the end of the law, so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes (Romans 10:4).

Anna, eighty-four years old, worships night and day with fasting and prayer, and speaks about the child to all who are waiting. Isaiah had promised a Servant who would be a light to the nations. Simeon and Anna see that light in a baby.

On this World Day for Consecrated Life let us thank God for our religious sisters, brothers and priests, presented to God like the child in the Temple. And let us keep awake, like Simeon and Anna, so that when the Lord comes we may recognize him and say: my eyes have seen your salvation. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was a tiny baby, Mary and Joseph took him to the Temple to give him to God. Old Simeon held him and was so happy!
Each morning you can also say: Jesus, I give you my day!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we enter the Great Fast. Moses was with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water (Exodus 34:28). When he came down, his face shone because he had been talking with God, and he did not even know it.
This is the purpose of the fast: not first to lose weight or to suffer, but to be with God, so that his light may begin to shine in us.

Isaiah warns that a fast can be empty. People fasted and quarrelled, fasted and oppressed their workers. God says: is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to share your bread with the hungry? (Isaiah 58:6–7). Then your light shall break forth like the dawn.

Paul tells us to put away the old self and clothe ourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God (Ephesians 4:22–24). The Great Fast is a change of clothes: the old self off, Christ on.

In the Gospel Jesus fasts forty days and is tempted three times: bread, a spectacle, power. Each time he answers with the word of God: one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God (Matthew 4:4). Where Adam and Israel failed, he stands firm.

We fast in him, and his victory is ours. Tonight, at Pethurtha, let us forgive one another at home. From tomorrow let us pray more, eat less, give more, and feed on God's word, so that at Easter our faces too may shine. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus did not eat for forty days, and when the devil tempted him, he said: God's word is more important than bread!
In the Great Fast, give up one sweet thing and say one extra prayer each day.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the first reading is a long list of names, and after almost every name the same words: and he died. But one man is different: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him (Genesis 5:24). He walked with God while raising sons and daughters, in an ordinary home.
That is the goal of the Great Fast. Not simply to give up fish and meat, but to walk with God, day after day, in our homes and at our work.

Israel crossed the Jordan and set up twelve stones, so that when the children asked, what do these stones mean?, the parents would tell them the story of God's mighty hand (Joshua 4:21–22). Our Lenten customs are such stones. When our children ask why we fast, let us tell them about Jesus.
Paul reminds us that everyone serves someone. For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord (Romans 6:23). Sin pays wages; God gives gifts.

Jesus warns us: not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father (Matthew 7:21). The two houses face the same storm. The difference is the foundation: the one who hears and acts has built on rock.
This week, let us choose one word of Jesus and do it. Let us dig down to the rock while the sky is clear. Then, when the storms come, our house will stand. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about a house on the rock and a house on the sand. When the rain came, only the house on the rock stood strong!
When we listen to Jesus and do what he says, we are building on the rock. What will you do this week?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the first reading tells us that the rain fell on the earth forty days and forty nights (Genesis 7:12). And before the waters rose, one small sentence: and the LORD shut him in (Genesis 7:16). Noah did not close the door himself. God did. Noah was saved because he was inside.
That is how we are saved in these forty days of the Great Fast. Not by our own swimming, but by staying inside the ark of the Church: in her sacraments, her prayer, her Sunday Qurbana.

Joshua near Jericho asks the commander of the LORD's army: are you for us or for our enemies? The answer is: neither (Joshua 5:13–14). The question is not whether God is on our side, but whether we are on his. Joshua removes his sandals and bows. And the walls of Jericho fall, not by force, but by a procession of prayer around the city.

Saint Paul cries out: I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I do. Wretched man that I am! Who will rescue me? And he answers: thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord (Romans 7:19, 24–25). Our rescue is a Person.

In the Gospel, while Jesus speaks of his cross, his disciples ask for the best seats. Jesus asks: are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? And he teaches: whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant; for the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many (Matthew 20:22, 26–28).
This week, let us stay inside the ark, walk around the walls of our sins in prayer, and choose the lowest place in order to serve. Then we will share his cup, and his glory. Amen.
kids: Children, God shut Noah and his family safe inside the ark when the big flood came. The Church is like the ark: inside, with Jesus, we are safe!
Jesus says that the greatest person is the one who serves others. How will you help someone at home this week without being asked?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the people of Babel say: come, let us build ourselves a city and a tower with its top in the heavens, and let us make a name for ourselves (Genesis 11:4). Their tower is so small that God has to come down to see it. Their project ends in confusion and scattering.

At Pentecost the Holy Spirit undoes Babel: people of every nation hear the apostles in their own language. Our Church prays in many languages across the world, but with one faith at one altar. Halfway through the fast, let us ask: for whose name am I building?

After Jericho, Israel is defeated at Ai, because one man has hidden stolen things in his tent. God tells Joshua: stand up; Israel has sinned (Joshua 7:10–11). One hidden sin weakened the whole camp. The Great Fast is the time to search our tents and bring what is hidden into the light of confession.

We do not do this as frightened slaves. Paul says: all who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God (Romans 8:14). We have received a spirit of adoption, and we cry: Abba! Father! We are heirs with Christ, if we suffer with him.

Jesus tells of tenants who beat the servants and kill the son of the owner, to seize the inheritance. He is speaking of his own death. But the stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone (Matthew 21:42). What men threw out of the vineyard, God made the foundation of everything.

We are tenants, not owners. Our faith, our families, our parishes are God's vineyard entrusted to us. This week, let us search our tents, pray the Our Father slowly as children, and give the Lord one real fruit. Amen.
kids: Children, people once tried to build a tower up to heaven to make themselves famous, but they ended up unable to understand each other! God wants us to build for his name, not ours.
Jesus is like a stone that the builders threw away, but God made him the most important stone of all. Let us build our lives on him!

homily: Dear friends, Paul asks the Thessalonians to pray that the word of the Lord may spread, because not all have faith. Then he adds: but the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one (2 Thessalonians 3:3).

In the Gospel a woman who has been ill for twelve years comes up behind Jesus. She thinks: if I only touch his cloak, I will be made well (Matthew 9:21). Jesus turns, looks at her and says: take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.
Then he goes to the house of the synagogue leader, whose daughter has died. The mourners laugh when he says she is sleeping. But he takes her by the hand, and the girl gets up.
Our faith may be as small as a touch. It is enough, because the one we touch is faithful. Let us reach out to him today, and let him direct our hearts to the love of God. Amen.
kids: Children, a sick lady touched just the edge of Jesus' clothes, and she was healed! Jesus loves it when we come to him with trust. What will you ask Jesus today?

homily: Dear friends, Paul charges Timothy: proclaim the message; be persistent whether the time is favorable or unfavorable (2 Timothy 4:2). People will look for teachers who say what their itching ears want to hear. But Timothy must do the work of an evangelist.
In the Gospel the Samaritan woman leaves her water jar and runs back to the city: come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done! She came for water and found the Messiah.
The disciples urge Jesus to eat. He says: my food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his work (John 4:34). Then he shows them the fields ripe for harvesting.
We reap what others have sown: the apostle Thomas, our missionaries, our parents and catechists. Let us thank them, leave our water jars, and say to someone: come and see. Amen.
kids: Children, a lady met Jesus at a well and was so happy that she forgot her water jar! She ran to tell everyone: come and see Jesus! Who can you tell about Jesus today?

homily: Dear friends, Peter tells us: regard the patience of our Lord as salvation (2 Peter 3:15). Every day that God waits is a day of mercy, given so that we may grow in the grace and knowledge of Christ.

Jesus asks us to show others the same patience: do not judge, and you will not be judged; do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven (Luke 6:37). The measure we give is the measure we get back.
Then he gives us a picture: someone with a log in his own eye trying to take a speck out of his neighbour's eye. First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly.

St John de Britto left the royal court of Portugal to live like a poor Tamil ascetic. He became all things to all people, and in 1693 he gave his life at Oriyur. May we, too, judge less, love more, and give ourselves in good measure. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a funny story about a man with a big log in his eye who wanted to take a tiny speck from his friend's eye! Let us look at our own faults first, and be kind to others.

homily: Dear friends, today, on the last Friday of Denha, we remember all the faithful departed. Ezekiel sees a valley full of dry bones, and God asks: mortal, can these bones live? (Ezekiel 37:3). When God's breath enters them, they live and stand up, a vast multitude.
Sirach praises our ancestors, the famous and the forgotten. Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lives on generation after generation (Sirach 44:14). God has forgotten none of them.

Paul tells us that the body is like a seed: it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power (1 Corinthians 15:43). We bury our dead in hope, because we believe in the resurrection of the body.

In the Gospel the King says: just as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me (Matthew 25:40). Let us serve Christ in the poor, pray for our departed, have the Holy Qurbana offered for them, and so prepare for the Great Fast that begins this Sunday. Amen.
kids: Children, God showed Ezekiel dry bones that came to life again! God will raise up our grandparents and everyone who loved him. Tonight, let us pray for our family members who have died.

homily: Dear friends, the risen Christ writes to the church of Laodicea: I know your works; you are neither cold nor hot (Revelation 3:15). They were rich and said: we need nothing. But they did not see that they were poor, blind and naked.

His words are hard, but they come from love: I reprove and discipline those whom I love. And then: listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you (Revelation 3:20).
In the Gospel great crowds bring the lame, the maimed, the blind and the mute and put them at Jesus' feet, and he cures them all. They did not pretend to be rich. They brought their poverty to him.
Tomorrow the Great Fast begins. Let us not be lukewarm. Let us admit our need, open the door with a good confession, and lay ourselves at his feet. Then he will come in and eat with us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: I am knocking at your door! When we pray and say sorry for our sins, we open the door, and Jesus comes in to be our friend. Will you open the door for Jesus?

homily: Dear friends, this morning the ash has marked our foreheads. The words remind us of the first sin and its sentence: you are dust, and to dust you shall return (Genesis 3:19). Yesterday was Pethurtha; the feasting is over, and the fifty days fast has begun.

But the Church gives us today the first page of the Bible. God speaks into the darkness: let there be light (Genesis 1:3). Again and again he looks at what he has made and sees that it is good. The fast does not despise God's gifts. It makes room for God to create us anew.

Like Joshua at the Jordan, we stand at the edge of a crossing. God says to us too: be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go (Joshua 1:9). And he gives us his word to carry, to meditate on day and night.

Jesus goes to the heart of the matter: if you remember at the altar that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there and go; first be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). Let the ash on our foreheads lead to peace in our homes. Then our fast will be pleasing to God. Amen.
kids: Children, today the priest put ash on our foreheads in the shape of a cross. It means: I belong to Jesus, and I want to start again. Is there someone you need to say sorry to today?

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we heard that we are dust. Today Genesis tells us what God does with dust: the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). We are dust, and we carry God's breath and image.

Paul warns us against judging others, because the judge is often doing the very same things. And he asks: do you not realize that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance? (Romans 2:4). God has been patient with us. That patience is an invitation to come home.

Jesus asks us to pass on that kindness: turn the other cheek; give your cloak as well; if anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). This is not weakness. It is the strength of love that does not answer evil with evil.
Let our fast become generous. What we save by fasting, let us give to the poor. And let us walk the second mile with someone who is difficult. Then God's image will shine in us again. Amen.
kids: Children, God made us from dust and breathed his own life into us. That is why every person is precious! Today, do one extra kind thing that nobody asked you to do.

homily: Dear friends, the first thing in creation that God calls not good is loneliness: it is not good that the man should be alone (Genesis 2:18). So God gives the man a partner, and the two become one flesh. We do not keep the Great Fast alone. We keep it as families, as a parish, as one Church.

Rahab, a woman of Jericho, hears what God has done and believes: the LORD your God is indeed God in heaven above and on earth below (Joshua 2:11). She ties a crimson cord in her window and is saved with her family. Paul reminds us that God wants doers of his word, not only hearers.

And Jesus teaches us how to pray: not to be seen, not with many words, but in the inner room. Go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret (Matthew 6:6). The Father knows what we need before we ask.
This Great Fast, let us find our inner room, and let our families pray together each evening. Then the Father who sees in secret will reward us. Amen.
kids: Children, you can talk to God anywhere, even in a quiet corner of your room. Shut the door, close your eyes and tell him what is in your heart. He is listening!

homily: Dear friends, the first sin began with a suspicion: that God was holding something back. Adam and Eve ate, their eyes were opened, and they hid. Then God came looking: where are you? (Genesis 3:9). He still asks that question, not to shame us, but to call us out of hiding.

Adam blamed the woman, and the woman blamed the serpent. Paul says that no one is righteous, not even one. The Great Fast begins when we stop blaming and say honestly: Lord, here I am, a sinner in need of you.

Joshua tells the people: sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you (Joshua 3:5). The ark of God goes first into the river. And Jesus tells us not to worry about food and clothing: look at the birds of the air; consider the lilies of the field.

When we fast we eat less, and we find that the Father still feeds us. So let us strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to us as well (Matthew 6:33). Amen.
kids: Children, God feeds the little birds and dresses the flowers in beautiful colours. He loves you even more! When you are worried, tell Jesus about it and trust him.

homily: Dear friends, God asked Adam: where are you? Today he asks Cain: where is your brother Abel? (Genesis 4:9). Sin against God soon becomes sin against the brother. Cain answers: am I my brother's keeper? God's answer is yes.

God had warned Cain: sin is lurking at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it (Genesis 4:7). Jealousy began with comparing. That is why Jesus says: do not judge. First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly (Matthew 7:5).
Abraham teaches us another way: hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). He did not look at his weakness but at God's promise. And Israel crossed the Jordan because God held back the waters.

Today is a Friday of the Great Fast. As we walk the Way of the Cross, we see the blood of Jesus, which speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. Let us become keepers of our brothers and sisters. Amen.
kids: Children, God asks each of us: where is your brother? where is your sister? Jesus wants us to take care of each other. Do something kind for your brother, sister or friend today.

homily: Dear friends, Paul says that all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus (Romans 3:23–24). Our fasting does not buy God's love. His love comes first.
So we fast with gratitude, not with pride. Our prayer, fasting and almsgiving are our answer to a gift already given, and God's grace makes even that answer possible.

Jesus gives us the prayer of the whole Great Fast: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name (Matthew 6:9). We pray it at the beginning of the Holy Qurbana and again before Communion. In it we ask for daily bread, for forgiveness, and for rescue in the time of trial.

Jesus explains one line only: if you forgive others, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). As this first week of the fast ends, let us forgive from the heart, so that we can pray this prayer honestly. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus taught us to call God our Father! Tonight, pray the Our Father slowly with your family, and think of someone you need to forgive.

homily: Dear friends, today Jesus says something surprising in the middle of our fast: nothing outside a person that goes in can defile, but the things that come out are what defile (Mark 7:15). Mark tells us that in this way Jesus declared all foods clean.
So why do we still give up fish and meat? Not because they are unclean. We give up good things so that our hearts learn to say no. The stomach becomes a teacher of the heart.

Jesus then names what really makes us unclean: evil intentions, theft, deceit, envy, slander, pride (Mark 7:21–22). These come from within. A fast that guards the kitchen but not the heart has guarded the wrong door.

And we cannot clean our hearts by ourselves. Saint Paul says that God saved us not because of our works but according to his mercy, through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). Let us ask him this week to keep our tongues gentle, to speak evil of no one, and to show every courtesy to everyone. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says that what makes us bad is not the food we eat but the unkind things that come out of our hearts and mouths. This week, can you fast from one unkind word?

homily: Dear friends, Saint Paul says that the whole creation has been groaning in labour pains until now (Romans 8:22). In these hot February days, when the fields are dry and the wells begin to fall, we can almost hear that groan. But it is the groan of a mother about to give birth, not of something dying.

We too groan as we wait. In this fast we feel hunger, we feel the pull of the habits we have given up. Paul says: in hope we were saved; and if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience (Romans 8:24–25).

Jesus teaches us how to wait: by prayer. Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you (Matthew 7:7). Our Father in heaven will never give us a stone when we ask for bread. He may not give what we name, but he always gives what is good.
And he ends with the golden rule: do to others as you would have them do to you (Matthew 7:12). Let us knock at God's door this week, and open our own door to others. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: ask, and you will receive. God is a good Father who loves to give good things. What will you ask him for today? And what good thing will you give to someone else?

homily: Dear friends, today some people carry a paralysed man to Jesus. He cannot come by himself. And the Gospel says: when Jesus saw their faith, he said, take heart, son; your sins are forgiven (Matthew 9:2). Their faith carried him.

The friends wanted healing for his legs, but Jesus heals his heart first. The deepest paralysis is sin, which keeps us from God. Then, to show that he has authority to forgive sins, Jesus tells the man: stand up, take your bed and go home (Matthew 9:6). And he does.

The crowd glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings (Matthew 9:8). That authority continues in the Church. When the priest says the words of absolution, it is Christ who says to us: your sins are forgiven.

Saint Paul tells us what the forgiven are to do: present your members as slaves to righteousness for sanctification (Romans 6:19). Let us go to confession this Lent, and let us carry someone else to Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, some friends carried a sick man to Jesus because they believed Jesus could help. Jesus forgave him and made him walk. Who can you help to come closer to Jesus this week?

homily: Dear friends, Saint Paul asks: if some people are unfaithful, does that cancel the faithfulness of God? By no means! Although everyone is a liar, let God be proved true (Romans 3:3–4). We have all broken promises, but God has never broken his.

Paul also rejects a dangerous idea: let us do evil so that good may come (Romans 3:8). The Church teaches that we may never do evil so that good may result. A good end does not make a lie or a bribe right.

Jesus then speaks about our everyday words. Do not swear at all, he says, not by heaven, not by the earth, not even by your own head (Matthew 5:34–36). We know how often we say, by my mother, by God, to make people believe us. Jesus wants us to be so truthful that no oath is needed.
Let your word be Yes, Yes or No, No (Matthew 5:37). This Lent, let us keep our promises, speak plainly and truly, and become like our faithful God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says we do not need to say “I promise on God” when we tell the truth. If we always tell the truth, everyone will believe our simple yes or no. Will you try to tell the truth always this week?

homily: Dear friends, Genesis tells us that when the wickedness of humankind became great, the LORD was sorry that he had made humankind, and it grieved him to his heart (Genesis 6:6). Sin is not only breaking a rule. It wounds the heart of God. And on this Friday, before the Cross, we see how far that wound went.
But Noah found favour in the sight of the LORD; he walked with God (Genesis 6:8–9). There is always a door of grace.

At Gilgal God said to his people: today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt (Joshua 5:9). They kept the Passover, and the manna ceased, because they had reached the land. When we go on pilgrimage this Lent, when we go to confession, the Lord rolls away our disgrace too.

In the Gospel the leaders answer Jesus: we do not know (Mark 11:33). They knew, but they did not want to change. Let us not hide behind those words. Let us say honestly what we know, and let the Lord change us. Amen.
kids: Children, the Bible says that sin makes God sad in his heart. Jesus loves us so much that he died on the Cross to take our sins away. Today, let us say sorry to Jesus and make his heart glad.

homily: Dear friends, Jesus compares his generation to children in the marketplace calling to one another: we played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we wailed, and you did not mourn (Matthew 11:17). They would join no game at all.

John fasted, and they said he had a demon. Jesus ate with sinners, and they called him a glutton and a drunkard (Matthew 11:18–19). The problem was not the music. It was hearts that had decided not to respond to God.

The Church gives us a time to mourn and a time to dance. Now is the time of the fast; Easter will be the time of the feast. Let us keep both with our whole heart. And when people mock our fast, let us not argue. Wisdom is vindicated by her deeds (Matthew 11:19).

Saint Paul reminds us to judge those inside before those outside (1 Corinthians 5:12). This Lent, let us first look honestly at ourselves, give up what enslaves us, and let the fruit of our fast speak for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about children who would not play any game, happy or sad. Let us not be like that with God! Now we are sorry for our sins, and at Easter we will be very happy. What good deed will you do today?

homily: Dear friends, we are in the third week of the Great Fast, when good resolutions grow tired. Paul reminds us that we have died to the old law through the body of Christ, so that we may belong to the risen Lord and serve in the new life of the Spirit (Romans 7:4–6).

A fast can be kept like a ledger: so many days without meat, so many prayers counted. Or it can be kept like a love: small gifts offered by a heart that belongs to Christ. Only the second bears fruit for God.

A scribe asks Jesus which commandment is first. Jesus answers: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength; and you shall love your neighbour as yourself (Mark 12:30–31).
The scribe understands, and Jesus tells him: you are not far from the kingdom of God (Mark 12:34). Let us not stay near the door. This week, let one choice each day be decided by love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said the most important rule is to love God with all your heart and to love others as you love yourself. Can you do one loving thing for God and one for someone at home today?

homily: Dear friends, Paul reminds us of Israel in the desert. They passed through the sea, they ate bread from heaven and drank from the rock, and the rock was Christ (1 Corinthians 10:4). Yet many of them fell, because they grumbled and turned away.
We too have been baptised and fed at the altar. These gifts are not a guarantee if we stop watching. So if you think you are standing, watch out that you do not fall (1 Corinthians 10:12).

But Paul gives us comfort: God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength, and with the testing he will provide the way out (1 Corinthians 10:13). There is always a way out, if we look for it.

Jesus warns us not to let our hearts be weighed down with too much pleasure, drink and worry. Be alert at all times, praying (Luke 21:36). Like St Polycarp, who served Christ for eighty-six years, may we watch and pray, and stand firm to the end. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asks us to stay awake inside, like a watchman at night. When something wrong tempts you, remember: God always gives you a way out. Ask him for it!

homily: Dear friends, Peter asks us for a tender heart and a humble mind. And he adds: do not repay evil for evil or abuse for abuse; but, on the contrary, repay with a blessing (1 Peter 3:9).

The world runs on the law of return. You hurt me, I hurt you. Peter asks us to break the circle. The Great Fast is also a fast of the tongue: a day without meat is easy compared with a day without a sharp reply.

Jesus goes further: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you (Matthew 5:44). God sends his sun and rain on the good and the bad alike. If we love only those who love us, what is special about that?

We may not feel love for an enemy, but we can pray for him. Prayer is where love begins. Jesus prayed on the Cross: Father, forgive them (Luke 23:34). Let us choose one name today, and pray for that person every day until Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asks us to pray even for people who are unkind to us. Tonight, can you say a little prayer for someone who was not nice to you? That is how God's children love!

homily: Dear friends, Paul speaks to parents and children, masters and servants. His key word is this: render service with enthusiasm, as to the Lord and not to men and women (Ephesians 6:7). Every honest work can be offered to Christ.

Jesus warns us about religion for show: those who like long robes and the best seats, who devour widows' houses and for the sake of appearance say long prayers (Mark 12:38–40). Even our fasting can become a show. Jesus wants service that protects the poor.

Today we remember Blessed Rani Maria, a Clarist sister from Pulluvazhy. At Udainagar near Indore she helped poor tribal families to learn, to save and to free themselves from moneylenders. On 25 February 1995 she was killed on a bus by a man hired by those she had angered. She was a sheep sent among wolves (Matthew 10:16).

Her killer repented in prison. Her sister tied a rakhi on his wrist and called him brother, and her parents welcomed him as a son. We carry the treasure of Christ in clay jars (2 Corinthians 4:7), but his power can make even a broken jar shine. Let us serve like Rani Maria, and forgive like her family. Amen.
kids: Children, Sister Rani Maria from Kerala went far away to help poor families learn to read and to be free. Some bad people killed her, but her family forgave the man who did it. Jesus' love is stronger than hate!

homily: Dear friends, after the flood God set his bow in the clouds as a sign of the covenant (Genesis 9:13). God hung up his weapon in the sky and promised: I will remember. Our God is a God who remembers his promises.

The walls of Jericho fell not by force but by obedience: seven days of walking in silence around the city, and then a shout. Lenten prayer is like that. We walk the Way of the Cross, Friday after Friday, and the walls of sin fall on a day we do not choose.

Paul gives us the most freeing word a sinner can hear: there is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus (Romans 8:1). Set your mind on the Spirit, and you will find life and peace.

Jesus tells the Sadducees that God is not God of the dead, but of the living (Mark 12:27). Our Way of the Cross ends at a tomb, but the tomb is not the end. Let us pray today for our departed, who are alive to God. Amen.
kids: Children, after the flood God put a rainbow in the sky as a promise. God always keeps his promises! And Jesus tells us that people who die in God's love are alive with him.

homily: Dear friends, Paul speaks to us about our everyday words. Speak the truth to your neighbours, for we are members of one another. Be angry but do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger (Ephesians 4:25–26).

Let no evil talk come out of your mouths, he says, but only words that build up and give grace to those who hear (Ephesians 4:29). Bitterness at the table grieves the Holy Spirit with whom we were sealed.
Jesus tells us of two sons. One says I will not, but later changes his mind and goes. The other says I go, sir, but does not go (Matthew 21:28–30). Which one did the will of his father?

Saying yes is not the same as going, and a past no is not the last word. The Great Fast is the time to change our minds. Let us make peace before the sun goes down, and go into the Father's vineyard today. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about two sons. One said no but then went to help his father. The other said yes but never went! Let us not only say yes to God, let us do it.

intro: Theme: “My eyes have seen your salvation.”
Mayaltho: the Lord enters his Temple, presented with the offering of the poor and received by those who waited.

q: Consecrate to me all the firstborn; whatever is the first to open the womb among the Israelites, of human beings and animals, is mine.
When the time came for their purification according to the law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord
points.apply: Offer yourself and your family to God at the start of each day.

sub: Light for the Gentiles, light for India.
q: I am the LORD, I have called you in righteousness, I have taken you by the hand and kept you; I have given you as a covenant to the people, a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, from the prison those who sit in darkness.

Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.
points.apply: Be gentle this week with someone who is bruised and weak.

points.h: A sign that will be opposed
sub: Christ, the end of the law.
q: See, I am laying in Zion a foundation stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation: “One who trusts will not panic.”

Then Simeon blessed them and said to his mother Mary, “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your own soul too.”
points.apply: When following Christ brings opposition, unite your pain with Mary's.

points.h: Fasting and prayer night and day
sub: The Lord comes to his temple.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.

She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day. At that moment she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
points.apply: Spend some quiet time before the Blessed Sacrament this week, waiting on the Lord.

concl: The Lord of the Temple came as a poor child, and only those who waited recognized him.
Keep awake with Simeon and Anna, and you too will see his salvation.
2027-02-02.resolve: Pray this week for consecrated persons, and thank one of them personally.

intro: Theme: “One does not live by bread alone.”
The Great Fast begins: forty days with God, the fast God chooses, victory over temptation, and the new self.

q: He was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.

And all of us, with unveiled faces, seeing the glory of the Lord as though reflected in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another; for this comes from the Lord, the Spirit.
points.apply: Set a fixed time of prayer every day of the Great Fast.

q: He humbled you by letting you hunger, then by feeding you with manna, with which neither you nor your ancestors were acquainted, in order to make you understand that one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
But he answered, “It is written, ‘One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
points.apply: Read one chapter of a Gospel every day of the Great Fast.
